---- MODULE W4Od10m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Blocks, PoolCap, NoBlock, NoRead

ASSUME NoBlock \notin Blocks

VARIABLES reg, snap, claim, powered, refused

Vars == <<reg, snap, claim, powered, refused>>

\* The substation pool can energise at most PoolCap track blocks at once.
\* The two line controllers share nothing but the register `reg`.
Energised == UNION {powered[c] : c \in Controllers}

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in 0..Cardinality(Blocks)
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> {NoRead} \union (0..Cardinality(Blocks))]
    /\ claim \in [Controllers -> {NoBlock} \union Blocks]
    /\ powered \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Blocks]
    /\ refused \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> NoRead]
    /\ claim = [c \in Controllers |-> NoBlock]
    /\ powered = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ refused = {}

\* A controller latches the register value it saw together with the block
\* it wants; that pair is its compare-and-swap expectation.
Latch(c, b) ==
    /\ snap[c] = NoRead
    /\ b \notin Energised
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered, refused>>

\* Headroom is judged from the latched snapshot, so the swap must also
\* confirm that nothing moved the register since the read.
Swap(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] < PoolCap
    /\ snap[c] = reg
    /\ claim[c] \notin Energised
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![c] = @ \union {claim[c]}]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED refused

\* Stale expectation: some other controller advanced the register first.
SwapFails(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] # reg
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered, refused>>

Refuse(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] >= PoolCap
    /\ snap[c] = reg
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ refused' = refused \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered>>

Deenergise(c, b) ==
    /\ b \in powered[c]
    /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {b}]
    /\ reg' = reg - 1
    /\ refused' = refused \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, claim>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : Latch(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Swap(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : SwapFails(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Refuse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : Deenergise(c, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Bounded capacity: the pool is never over-drawn, however the two
\* independent controllers interleave their latch/swap attempts.
PoolNeverOverdrawn == Cardinality(Energised) <= PoolCap
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {northline, southline}
    Blocks = {bkA, bkB, bkC}
    PoolCap = 2
    NoBlock = nb
    NoRead = nr

INVARIANT PoolNeverOverdrawn
nl:
A metropolitan subway runs two line controllers -- one for the north line, one for the south line -- that schedule train movements completely independently of one another. Both draw traction current for the track blocks they energise from a single shared substation pool, and that pool can energise at most PoolCap blocks at any instant. There is no lock between the controllers; their only shared state is a compare-and-swap register holding the number of blocks currently energised.

A controller admits a train into a block in two steps. First it latches: it reads the register into its own private snapshot and records which block it intends to energise, which is only allowed if that block is not already energised by anybody. Then it swaps: it decides from its latched snapshot whether the pool still has headroom, and commits only if the register is still equal to that snapshot. If the register has moved since the read, the swap fails, and the controller discards its snapshot and its claim so it can start over. If the snapshot is current but already sits at the pool limit, the controller instead marks itself as refused and abandons the attempt. Independently of all that, a controller may de-energise any block it currently holds, which decrements the register and clears that controller's own refused mark.

The crucial detail is that the headroom decision is made against the latched snapshot rather than against the live register. Only the compare-and-swap step stops two controllers from both concluding there is room for one more train and both drawing current for it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The two line controllers together never hold more than PoolCap energised blocks at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od7m7p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Planners, Ships, HoldCap, NoShip

ASSUME NoShip \notin Ships

VARIABLES phase, stamp, stowed, latchShip, latchStamp, manifest

Vars == <<phase, stamp, stowed, latchShip, latchStamp, manifest>>

\* Two independent planner instances drive one shared pool of berth
\* registers.  A register carries a version stamp that every write advances,
\* and that stamp is the only evidence a planner has that its latched view
\* of a ship is still current.
Orders(s) == Cardinality({i \in 1..Len(manifest) : manifest[i] = s})

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Ships -> {"stowing", "cleared", "sailed"}]
    /\ stamp \in [Ships -> 0..2]
    /\ stowed \in [Ships -> 0..HoldCap]
    /\ latchShip \in [Planners -> {NoShip} \union Ships]
    /\ latchStamp \in [Planners -> 0..2]
    /\ manifest \in Seq(Ships)

Init ==
    /\ phase = [s \in Ships |-> "stowing"]
    /\ stamp = [s \in Ships |-> 0]
    /\ stowed = [s \in Ships |-> 0]
    /\ latchShip = [p \in Planners |-> NoShip]
    /\ latchStamp = [p \in Planners |-> 0]
    /\ manifest = <<>>

Stow(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "stowing"
    /\ stowed[s] < HoldCap
    /\ stowed' = [stowed EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, stamp, latchShip, latchStamp, manifest>>

ClearForSea(s) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "stowing"
    /\ stowed[s] = HoldCap
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "cleared"]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stowed, latchShip, latchStamp, manifest>>

\* One indivisible peek records both the ship and the stamp behind it.
Latch(p, s) ==
    /\ latchShip[p] = NoShip
    /\ phase[s] = "cleared"
    /\ latchShip' = [latchShip EXCEPT ![p] = s]
    /\ latchStamp' = [latchStamp EXCEPT ![p] = stamp[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, stamp, stowed, manifest>>

\* The commit never re-reads the phase; it swaps on the stamp alone.
IssueSailingOrder(p) ==
    /\ latchShip[p] # NoShip
    /\ latchStamp[p] = stamp[latchShip[p]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![latchShip[p]] = "sailed"]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![latchShip[p]] = @ + 1]
    /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, latchShip[p])
    /\ latchShip' = [latchShip EXCEPT ![p] = NoShip]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stowed, latchStamp>>

DropStaleLatch(p) ==
    /\ latchShip[p] # NoShip
    /\ latchStamp[p] # stamp[latchShip[p]]
    /\ latchShip' = [latchShip EXCEPT ![p] = NoShip]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, stamp, stowed, latchStamp, manifest>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Ships : Stow(s)
    \/ \E s \in Ships : ClearForSea(s)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, s \in Ships : Latch(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : IssueSailingOrder(p)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : DropStaleLatch(p)

\* Planners are not required to be prompt about stowing, but a planner that
\* can advance a berth register must eventually do so.
PlannerStep ==
    \/ \E p \in Planners, s \in Ships : Latch(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : IssueSailingOrder(p)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : DropStaleLatch(p)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(PlannerStep)

\* Irreversibility: the manifest entry for a ship can never be duplicated,
\* however the two planners interleave their latches and commits.
OrderIssuedAtMostOnce == \A s \in Ships : Orders(s) <= 1

\* Progress: a cleared ship is not abandoned at the berth.
EveryClearedShipSails ==
    \A s \in Ships : (phase[s] = "cleared") ~> (phase[s] = "sailed")
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Planners = {yardA, yardB}
    Ships = {mvAurora, mvBoreas}
    HoldCap = 2
    NoShip = noship

INVARIANT OrderIssuedAtMostOnce
PROPERTY EveryClearedShipSails

\* Once every ship has sailed the yard is quiescent, which is a legitimate
\* terminal state rather than a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs two independent instances of its planning service, yardA and yardB, brought up as a pair so that neither is a single point of failure. They do not talk to each other. Both operate on one shared pool of berth registers, one register per ship, and each register holds the ship's phase together with a version stamp that is advanced by every write to that register.

A ship starts in the stowing phase with an empty hold. A crane may stow one more container onto a stowing ship as long as its hold is not yet full. Once a stowing ship's hold is exactly full, the yard clears it for sea, which moves it to the cleared phase and advances its stamp. Issuing the sailing order is the irreversible step: once a ship has sailed, its entry is on the port's departure manifest permanently and there is no way to recall it or amend the manifest.

A planner issues a sailing order in two stages. First it latches: in one indivisible peek it records the identity of a cleared ship together with the stamp it read from that ship's register. Later it commits: it writes the sailed phase, advances the stamp again, and appends the ship to the departure manifest, but only if the stamp it latched still matches the stamp in the register. If the stamp no longer matches, the other planner got there first, so the latch is stale and the planner simply drops it and moves on. Note that the commit stage never re-reads the phase; the stamp comparison is the only thing that tells a planner its latched view of the ship is still current.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No ship is ever appended to the departure manifest more than once, even when both planner instances latch the same cleared ship.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ship that reaches the cleared phase eventually sails rather than being left indefinitely at the berth.

---- MODULE W4Od13m6p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Techs, Hopper, DepotSize, MaxEpoch, NoTech, NoMachine

VARIABLES stock, holder, epoch, plan, depot

Vars == <<stock, holder, epoch, plan, depot>>

\* A restocking lease names one technician and carries the machine's epoch.
\* Every grant and every expiry bumps that epoch, so the epoch a technician
\* was handed is its only evidence that the headroom it measured is still
\* its own to fill.
Idle(t) == plan[t].mc = NoMachine

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in [Machines -> 0..(2 * Hopper)]
    /\ holder \in [Machines -> {NoTech} \union Techs]
    /\ epoch \in [Machines -> Nat]
    /\ plan \in [Techs -> [mc: {NoMachine} \union Machines, ep: Nat,
                           qty: 0..Hopper]]
    /\ depot \in 0..DepotSize

Init ==
    /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ holder = [m \in Machines |-> NoTech]
    /\ epoch = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ plan = [t \in Techs |-> [mc |-> NoMachine, ep |-> 0, qty |-> 0]]
    /\ depot = DepotSize

GrantLease(m, t) ==
    /\ holder[m] = NoTech
    /\ Idle(t)
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m] = t]
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![t] = [mc |-> m, ep |-> epoch[m] + 1, qty |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, depot>>

\* Headroom is measured once, when the van is loaded, and never again.
LoadVan(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ plan[t].qty = 0
    /\ LET need == Hopper - stock[plan[t].mc]
       IN  /\ need > 0
           /\ need <= depot
           /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![t].qty = need]
           /\ depot' = depot - need
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, holder, epoch>>

\* Expiry is unilateral and runs on the machine's clock; the technician is
\* merely slow, still on the road and still going to turn up.
ExpireLease(m) ==
    /\ holder[m] # NoTech
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m] = NoTech]
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, plan, depot>>

TopUp(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ plan[t].qty > 0
    /\ plan[t].ep = epoch[plan[t].mc]
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![plan[t].mc] = @ + plan[t].qty]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![t] = [mc |-> NoMachine, ep |-> 0, qty |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, depot>>

\* A technician whose lease moved on returns its untouched cans.
StandDown(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ plan[t].ep # epoch[plan[t].mc]
    /\ depot' = depot + plan[t].qty
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![t] = [mc |-> NoMachine, ep |-> 0, qty |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, holder, epoch>>

Vend(m) ==
    /\ stock[m] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, plan, depot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines, t \in Techs : GrantLease(m, t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : LoadVan(t)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : ExpireLease(m)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : TopUp(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : StandDown(t)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Vend(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Lease churn is the only unbounded dimension of this model, so capping the
\* epoch is what keeps it finite; it hides no over-fill.
EpochBound == \A m \in Machines : epoch[m] <= MaxEpoch

\* Bounded capacity: a hopper is never filled past its rating, even when a
\* lease expires under a technician who has already drawn cans against the
\* headroom figure it read before the hand-over.
HopperWithinCapacity == \A m \in Machines : stock[m] <= Hopper
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vmLobby, vmGym}
    Techs = {techRae, techMoss}
    Hopper = 2
    DepotSize = 4
    MaxEpoch = 5
    NoTech = notech
    NoMachine = nomachine

CONSTRAINT EpochBound

INVARIANT HopperWithinCapacity
nl:
A regional operator runs a network of vending machines that are refilled by roving field technicians. Each machine has a rated hopper capacity and must never be filled past it, because a jammed over-full hopper takes the machine out of service. Cans come from one shared regional depot with a finite stock on hand.

Refilling is coordinated by leases rather than by any central dispatcher. A machine hands its restocking lease to one idle technician at a time and stamps the lease with the machine's current epoch number; every grant and every expiry bumps that epoch. The technician records the machine, the epoch it was handed, and an initially empty load. The technician then loads its van exactly once: it measures the machine's headroom at that moment, draws that many cans out of the depot, and drives out.

Leases expire on the machine's own clock, not the technician's. When a lease expires the machine simply drops its holder and bumps its epoch. The technician is slow rather than failed -- it is still on the road and will still turn up -- so a machine whose lease has expired is free to hand a fresh lease to somebody else, who will measure headroom against whatever the hopper holds by then.

When a technician arrives it tops up: it adds the load it is carrying to the machine's stock, but only if the epoch it was handed still matches the machine's epoch. It never re-measures headroom on arrival; the headroom figure it is acting on is the one it took when it loaded the van. A technician that finds the epoch has moved on stands down instead, returning its untouched cans to the depot. Independently of all this, any machine with stock in it can vend one item to a customer.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No machine's hopper ever holds more than its rated capacity, even when a lease expires under a technician who has already loaded a van against the old headroom figure.

---- MODULE W4Od0m6p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Rooms, Teams, Cases, AnaesCap, NoTeam, NoCase

ASSUME NoCase \notin Cases

VARIABLES waiting, inTheatre, poolHolder, booking, chiefLog

Vars == <<waiting, inTheatre, poolHolder, booking, chiefLog>>

\* The scarce resource is anaesthesia coverage, not theatre space: there are
\* more rooms than the service can staff.  A team's headroom figure is taken
\* once, when it receives the pool lease, and is never refreshed.
Busy == {r \in Rooms : inTheatre[r] # NoCase}

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \subseteq Cases
    /\ inTheatre \in [Rooms -> {NoCase} \union Cases]
    /\ poolHolder \in {NoTeam} \union Teams
    /\ booking \in [Teams -> [seen: 0..Cardinality(Rooms), held: BOOLEAN]]
    /\ chiefLog \subseteq Cases

Init ==
    /\ waiting = Cases
    /\ inTheatre = [r \in Rooms |-> NoCase]
    /\ poolHolder = NoTeam
    /\ booking = [t \in Teams |-> [seen |-> 0, held |-> FALSE]]
    /\ chiefLog = {}

TakePoolLease(t) ==
    /\ poolHolder = NoTeam
    /\ ~booking[t].held
    /\ waiting # {}
    /\ poolHolder' = t
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![t] = [seen |-> Cardinality(Busy),
                                          held |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inTheatre, chiefLog>>

\* The lease clock, not the team, decides when the lease lapses; the team is
\* slow rather than gone and is never told.
LapsePoolLease ==
    /\ poolHolder # NoTeam
    /\ poolHolder' = NoTeam
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inTheatre, booking, chiefLog>>

\* Still the recorded holder, and the stale headroom figure still under the
\* cap: those two together are what license opening a case.
OpenCase(t, c, r) ==
    /\ booking[t].held
    /\ poolHolder = t
    /\ booking[t].seen < AnaesCap
    /\ c \in waiting
    /\ inTheatre[r] = NoCase
    /\ inTheatre' = [inTheatre EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![t].held = FALSE]
    /\ poolHolder' = NoTeam
    /\ UNCHANGED chiefLog

StandDown(t) ==
    /\ booking[t].held
    /\ \/ poolHolder # t
       \/ booking[t].seen >= AnaesCap
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![t].held = FALSE]
    /\ poolHolder' = IF poolHolder = t THEN NoTeam ELSE poolHolder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inTheatre, chiefLog>>

CloseCase(r) ==
    /\ inTheatre[r] # NoCase
    /\ inTheatre' = [inTheatre EXCEPT ![r] = NoCase]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, poolHolder, booking, chiefLog>>

\* Two privileged powers that skip admission control altogether.
ChiefTransferOut(c) ==
    /\ c \in waiting
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
    /\ chiefLog' = chiefLog \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTheatre, poolHolder, booking>>

ChiefClearTheatre(r) ==
    /\ inTheatre[r] # NoCase
    /\ chiefLog' = chiefLog \union {inTheatre[r]}
    /\ inTheatre' = [inTheatre EXCEPT ![r] = NoCase]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, poolHolder, booking>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams : TakePoolLease(t)
    \/ LapsePoolLease
    \/ \E t \in Teams, c \in Cases, r \in Rooms : OpenCase(t, c, r)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : StandDown(t)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : CloseCase(r)
    \/ \E c \in Cases : ChiefTransferOut(c)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : ChiefClearTheatre(r)

LeaseStep ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams : TakePoolLease(t)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : StandDown(t)

TheatreStep == \E r \in Rooms : CloseCase(r)

AdmitStep == \E t \in Teams, c \in Cases, r \in Rooms : OpenCase(t, c, r)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(LeaseStep)
    /\ WF_Vars(TheatreStep)
    /\ SF_Vars(AdmitStep)

\* Bounded capacity: never more concurrent operations than the anaesthesia
\* service can cover, however leases lapse under preparing teams.
CoverageNotOverdrawn == Cardinality(Busy) <= AnaesCap

\* Progress: the day's list is not left half-scheduled forever.
WaitingListDrains == <>(waiting = {})
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Rooms = {orNorth, orSouth, orAnnex}
    Teams = {teamVas, teamOrtho}
    Cases = {caseA, caseB, caseC}
    AnaesCap = 2
    NoTeam = noteam
    NoCase = nocase

INVARIANT CoverageNotOverdrawn
PROPERTY WaitingListDrains

\* An empty waiting list with every theatre clear is the end of the day's
\* list, not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital schedules its operating rooms around a scarce resource that is not the rooms themselves: the anaesthesia service can cover only AnaesCap concurrent operations, no matter how many theatres stand empty. The scheduler therefore has more theatres than the anaesthesia service can staff, and its whole job is to never start more operations at once than the service can cover.

Admission is regulated by a single lease on the anaesthesia pool. A surgical team that wants to open a case takes the pool lease when it is free and there is still something on the waiting list; at the instant the lease is handed over, the team writes down how many theatres it saw occupied. That figure is the team's headroom estimate and it is never refreshed. The pool lease expires on its own clock: the lease is simply dropped, and the team that was holding it is not notified and has not failed -- it is still preparing and will still come back.

To open a case the team must find that it is still the recorded holder of the pool lease, that the headroom figure it wrote down is below the anaesthesia cap, that the case is still on the waiting list, and that some theatre is empty. It then moves the case into that theatre and gives the lease back. A team that comes back to find the lease is no longer recorded in its name, or that its own headroom figure had already reached the cap, stands down instead, releasing the lease if it still holds it. Any operation in progress can finish normally, which empties its theatre.

The chief of surgery has two privileged powers that bypass admission control entirely. The chief can transfer a waiting case out to another hospital without taking the lease at all, and the chief can order a theatre cleared immediately, ending an operation early. Both chief actions are written to the chief's order log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of operations in progress at any moment never exceeds the anaesthesia service's concurrent-coverage cap.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The waiting list is eventually emptied -- every scheduled case is eventually either taken into a theatre or transferred out by chief order.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m3p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Branches, Titles, MaxTerm, MaxJournal, NoBranch, NoConf

VARIABLES term, coord, believes, outbound, journal, served

Vars == <<term, coord, believes, outbound, journal, served>>

\* `believes[b]` is never invalidated, so a superseded branch still thinks it
\* holds its old term.  The registry's two acceptance tests are the only
\* thing standing between that stale belief and the permanent journal.
Conf == [ttl: Titles, tm: 0..MaxTerm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ coord \in {NoBranch} \union Branches
    /\ believes \in [Branches -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ outbound \in [Branches -> {NoConf} \union Conf]
    /\ journal \in Seq(0..MaxTerm)
    /\ served \subseteq Titles

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ coord = NoBranch
    /\ believes = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ outbound = [b \in Branches |-> NoConf]
    /\ journal = <<>>
    /\ served = {}

Recognise(b) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ coord # b
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ coord' = b
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![b] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<outbound, journal, served>>

\* Failover leaves the registry with no coordinator at all for a while.
StandDown ==
    /\ coord # NoBranch
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ coord' = NoBranch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believes, outbound, journal, served>>

\* A branch stamps its own remembered term, which may be long superseded.
QueueConf(b, t) ==
    /\ believes[b] > 0
    /\ outbound[b] = NoConf
    /\ outbound' = [outbound EXCEPT ![b] = [ttl |-> t, tm |-> believes[b]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, believes, journal, served>>

\* The registry may pick up branch outboxes in any order, so this is where
\* reordering can put an older term behind a newer one.
Accept(b) ==
    /\ outbound[b] # NoConf
    /\ outbound[b].tm = term
    /\ coord = b
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, outbound[b].tm)
    /\ served' = served \union {outbound[b].ttl}
    /\ outbound' = [outbound EXCEPT ![b] = NoConf]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, believes>>

Drop(b) ==
    /\ outbound[b] # NoConf
    /\ \/ outbound[b].tm # term
       \/ coord # b
    /\ outbound' = [outbound EXCEPT ![b] = NoConf]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, believes, journal, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Recognise(b)
    \/ StandDown
    \/ \E b \in Branches, t \in Titles : QueueConf(b, t)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Accept(b)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Drop(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* The journal is the only unbounded dimension of the model, so capping its
\* length is what keeps this finite.
JournalBound == Len(journal) <= MaxJournal

\* No stale participant acts: reading down the permanent journal, the terms
\* never go backwards.
JournalTermsNeverRegress ==
    \A i \in 1..(Len(journal) - 1) : journal[i] <= journal[i + 1]

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Branches = {brElm, brOak}
    Titles = {tlHobbit, tlDune}
    MaxTerm = 3
    MaxJournal = 3
    NoBranch = nobranch
    NoConf = noconf

CONSTRAINT JournalBound

INVARIANT JournalTermsNeverRegress
nl:
A county library runs its book-reservation service from several branch servers, one of which is recognised at any time as the reservation coordinator. Recognition is held in a shared registry that records the current coordinator together with a term number; the term number is bumped every time recognition changes hands. Each branch server separately remembers the term in which it was last told it had been recognised, and that memory is never invalidated -- a server that has quietly been superseded still believes it is the coordinator.

Confirmations travel over the branch network, which does not preserve order. Each branch holds at most one confirmation outbound at a time, stamped with the term the branch believes it holds. The registry may pick up outbound confirmations from the branches in any order, so an older branch's confirmation can be picked up after a newer branch's.

The registry appends every accepted reservation to a permanent reservation journal, recording the term under which it was accepted, and marks the title as served. Acceptance is conditional: the registry accepts a confirmation only if the stamped term equals the registry's current term and the sending branch is the branch the registry currently recognises. A confirmation that fails either test is dropped.

There are four other things the system does. Recognition can move to a branch that is not currently recognised, which bumps the term and tells that branch it holds the new term. The recognised coordinator can be stood down, which bumps the term and leaves the registry with no coordinator at all until the next recognition. A branch that believes it holds a term can queue an outbound confirmation for any title. And any queued confirmation that fails the two acceptance tests is dropped.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The term numbers recorded down the reservation journal never decrease, so no superseded branch's confirmation is ever journalled after a later term's confirmation has been journalled.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Fridges, Trackers, StockTotal, RetryBudget, NoMove

VARIABLES units, version, txn, batch, retries, writtenOff

Vars == <<units, version, txn, batch, retries, writtenOff>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

\* A requested move is an ordered pair of distinct fridges.
Moves == {m \in Fridges \X Fridges : m[1] # m[2]}

Idle(t) == txn[t].mv = NoMove

TypeOK ==
    /\ units \in [Fridges -> 0..(2 * StockTotal)]
    /\ version \in Nat
    /\ txn \in [Trackers -> [mv: {NoMove} \union Moves, vsn: Nat,
                             snap: 0..(2 * StockTotal)]]
    /\ batch \subseteq Moves
    /\ retries \in [Trackers -> 0..RetryBudget]
    /\ writtenOff \in 0..StockTotal

Init ==
    /\ units = [f \in Fridges |-> IF f = CHOOSE g \in Fridges : TRUE
                                  THEN StockTotal ELSE 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ txn = [t \in Trackers |-> [mv |-> NoMove, vsn |-> 0, snap |-> 0]]
    /\ batch = Moves
    /\ retries = [t \in Trackers |-> 0]
    /\ writtenOff = 0

\* The snapshot fixes both the version and the source count.
Begin(t, m) ==
    /\ Idle(t)
    /\ m \in batch
    /\ units[m[1]] > 0
    /\ txn' = [txn EXCEPT ![t] = [mv |-> m, vsn |-> version,
                                  snap |-> units[m[1]]]]
    /\ batch' = batch \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, version, retries, writtenOff>>

\* The source side is written as an absolute value derived from the stale
\* snapshot; only the version test makes that safe.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ txn[t].vsn = version
    /\ units' = [units EXCEPT ![txn[t].mv[1]] = txn[t].snap - 1,
                              ![txn[t].mv[2]] = units[txn[t].mv[2]] + 1]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ txn' = [txn EXCEPT ![t] = [mv |-> NoMove, vsn |-> 0, snap |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, retries, writtenOff>>

Retry(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ txn[t].vsn # version
    /\ retries[t] < RetryBudget
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ batch' = batch \union {txn[t].mv}
    /\ txn' = [txn EXCEPT ![t] = [mv |-> NoMove, vsn |-> 0, snap |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, version, writtenOff>>

Abandon(t) ==
    /\ ~Idle(t)
    /\ txn[t].vsn # version
    /\ retries[t] = RetryBudget
    /\ txn' = [txn EXCEPT ![t] = [mv |-> NoMove, vsn |-> 0, snap |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, version, batch, retries, writtenOff>>

Cancel(m) ==
    /\ m \in batch
    /\ units[m[1]] = 0
    /\ batch' = batch \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, version, txn, retries, writtenOff>>

WriteOff(f) ==
    /\ units[f] > 0
    /\ writtenOff < StockTotal
    /\ units' = [units EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ writtenOff' = writtenOff + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, batch, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trackers, m \in Moves : Begin(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Retry(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Abandon(t)
    \/ \E m \in Moves : Cancel(m)
    \/ \E f \in Fridges : WriteOff(f)

TrackerStep ==
    \/ \E t \in Trackers, m \in Moves : Begin(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Retry(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trackers : Abandon(t)
    \/ \E m \in Moves : Cancel(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(TrackerStep)

\* Conservation: fridge contents plus the written-off tally always equal the
\* stock the shift opened with.
StockConserved == Tally(units, Fridges) + writtenOff = StockTotal

\* Progress: the batch empties and no instance is left mid-transfer.
BatchSettled == <>(batch = {} /\ \A t \in Trackers : Idle(t))
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Fridges = {frIntake, frWard}
    Trackers = {trkPrimary, trkStandby}
    StockTotal = 3
    RetryBudget = 1
    NoMove = nomove

INVARIANT StockConserved
PROPERTY BatchSettled

\* A settled batch with nothing left to write off is the end of the shift,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital blood bank keeps its units in a small number of fridges and tracks them with two independently deployed instances of the same inventory tracker. The two instances were brought up separately for redundancy and do not coordinate with each other; they read and write one shared inventory record covering every fridge. Every unit of blood is accounted for: a unit is either sitting in a fridge or has been formally written off as expired. Nothing may be conjured up and nothing may quietly vanish.

The shared record carries a version number that is bumped by every write to it. There is a fixed batch of requested transfers for the shift, each naming a source fridge and a destination fridge, and either tracker instance may pick up any of them. Each instance also has a fixed retry budget for the shift.

An instance begins a transfer by taking a requested move out of the batch and reading a snapshot: it records the version it saw and the count it saw at the source fridge. It commits by writing the source fridge's count back as its snapshot count minus one and adding one to whatever the destination fridge holds at that moment -- so the source side of the write is an absolute value computed from the old snapshot, not a decrement applied to the current value. The commit is only allowed if the version number is still the one the instance read.

If the version has moved on, the instance's snapshot is out of date. With retry budget left it burns one retry and puts the move back in the batch for another attempt; with the budget exhausted it abandons the move for the shift. A requested move whose source fridge is empty is cancelled outright. Separately, either instance may write off one unit from any non-empty fridge as expired, which bumps the version and moves that unit into the written-off tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units sitting in the fridges plus the units written off as expired always add up to exactly the stock the shift started with, so no unit is ever created or destroyed by a transfer.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The shift's transfer batch is eventually settled -- the batch empties and neither tracker instance is left holding a half-finished transfer.

---- MODULE W4Od8m8p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Depts, Codes, Workers, Chartered, NoWorker, NoSection

\* A section is identified by its department and its course code, so the
\* coarse handle a worker needs is read straight off the section itself.
Sections == Depts \X Codes

DeptOf(s) == s[1]

VARIABLES free, filled, deptHandle, sectHandle, outstanding

Vars == <<free, filled, deptHandle, sectHandle, outstanding>>

Quiet(d) == \A s \in Sections : DeptOf(s) = d => sectHandle[s] = NoWorker

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in [Sections -> 0..(2 * Chartered)]
    /\ filled \in [Sections -> 0..(2 * Chartered)]
    /\ deptHandle \in [Depts -> {NoWorker} \union Workers]
    /\ sectHandle \in [Sections -> {NoWorker} \union Workers]
    /\ outstanding \in [Workers -> [sec: {NoSection} \union Sections,
                                    reading: 0..(2 * Chartered)]]

Init ==
    /\ free = [s \in Sections |-> Chartered]
    /\ filled = [s \in Sections |-> 0]
    /\ deptHandle = [d \in Depts |-> NoWorker]
    /\ sectHandle = [s \in Sections |-> NoWorker]
    /\ outstanding = [w \in Workers |-> [sec |-> NoSection, reading |-> 0]]

ClaimDept(w, d) ==
    /\ deptHandle[d] = NoWorker
    /\ outstanding[w].sec = NoSection
    /\ deptHandle' = [deptHandle EXCEPT ![d] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, filled, sectHandle, outstanding>>

\* Coarse then fine: the section handle is only reachable through the
\* department handle, and taking it is also when the reading is written down.
\* The coarse handle then goes straight back; the fine handle does not.
ClaimSection(w, s) ==
    /\ deptHandle[DeptOf(s)] = w
    /\ sectHandle[s] = NoWorker
    /\ outstanding[w].sec = NoSection
    /\ free[s] > 0
    /\ sectHandle' = [sectHandle EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![w] = [sec |-> s,
                                                  reading |-> free[s]]]
    /\ deptHandle' = [deptHandle EXCEPT ![DeptOf(s)] = NoWorker]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, filled>>

\* The free count is written back from the reading, not decremented from the
\* current value; outstanding registrations post in no particular order.
PostRegistration(w) ==
    /\ outstanding[w].sec # NoSection
    /\ LET s == outstanding[w].sec
       IN  /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![s] = outstanding[w].reading - 1]
           /\ filled' = [filled EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
           /\ sectHandle' = [sectHandle EXCEPT ![s] = NoWorker]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![w] = [sec |-> NoSection,
                                                  reading |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED deptHandle

Withdraw(w) ==
    /\ outstanding[w].sec # NoSection
    /\ sectHandle' = [sectHandle EXCEPT ![outstanding[w].sec] = NoWorker]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![w] = [sec |-> NoSection,
                                                  reading |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, filled, deptHandle>>

\* The coarse-level action, and the reason the coarse level exists: it may
\* only run when no fine handle in the department is out, because an
\* outstanding registration still holds a reading this would invalidate.
ReleaseDeptSeats(w, d) ==
    /\ deptHandle[d] = w
    /\ Quiet(d)
    /\ free' = [s \in Sections |-> IF DeptOf(s) = d /\ filled[s] > 0
                                   THEN free[s] + 1 ELSE free[s]]
    /\ filled' = [s \in Sections |-> IF DeptOf(s) = d /\ filled[s] > 0
                                     THEN filled[s] - 1 ELSE filled[s]]
    /\ deptHandle' = [deptHandle EXCEPT ![d] = NoWorker]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sectHandle, outstanding>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers, d \in Depts : ClaimDept(w, d)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Sections : ClaimSection(w, s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : PostRegistration(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Withdraw(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, d \in Depts : ReleaseDeptSeats(w, d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: every section's seats are all still accounted for, none
\* minted by a post that worked from a reading somebody else invalidated.
SeatsConserved == \A s \in Sections : free[s] + filled[s] = Chartered
====
nl:
A university course-registration system is operated by a pool of registrar workers. Every teaching section belongs to exactly one department, and each section's seats are accounted for exactly: a seat is either free or filled, and the two figures must always add up to the section's chartered capacity. Seats are neither minted nor lost -- a section that is chartered for a certain number of seats has that many seats forever.

Because a section can only be touched through its department, the workers acquire the two levels in order: coarse first, then fine. A worker with no outstanding work claims a department's handle when that handle is free. Holding a department handle, the worker may then claim the handle of one section in that department, provided the section handle is free and the section still has a free seat. Claiming the section handle is also when the worker takes its reading: it writes down the section's free-seat figure. Having taken the reading, the worker gives the department handle straight back -- so other workers can get on with other departments -- but keeps the section handle for as long as its registration is outstanding.

Registrations post asynchronously and the registrar makes no promise about the order in which outstanding registrations from different workers land. Posting a registration writes the section's free-seat count back as the figure the worker wrote down minus one, and adds one to whatever the filled count is at that moment; the section handle is then released. A worker may instead withdraw its outstanding registration, releasing the section handle and writing nothing.

There is one department-wide administrative action. A worker holding a department handle may release one filled seat back to free in every section of that department at once -- but only if no section handle anywhere in that department is currently claimed, because an outstanding registration is still working from a free-seat figure that this action would invalidate.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every section, the free-seat count plus the filled-seat count always equals that section's chartered capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Scripts, Quorum, MaxRound

VARIABLES queue, licensed, round, tally, dispensed, overridden

Vars == <<queue, licensed, round, tally, dispensed, overridden>>

\* A ballot carries the round it was cast in, so the cabinet can tell a live
\* approval from the residue of a roll that has since changed.
Ballot == [ph: Pharmacists, rnd: 0..MaxRound]

Voted(p) == \E b \in tally : b.ph = p

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \subseteq Scripts
    /\ licensed \subseteq Pharmacists
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ tally \subseteq Ballot
    /\ dispensed \subseteq Scripts
    /\ overridden \subseteq Scripts

Init ==
    /\ queue = Scripts
    /\ licensed = Pharmacists
    /\ round = 0
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ dispensed = {}
    /\ overridden = {}

CastBallot(p) ==
    /\ p \in licensed
    /\ ~Voted(p)
    /\ tally' = tally \union {[ph |-> p, rnd |-> round]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, licensed, round, dispensed, overridden>>

Dispense(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed \union {s}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<licensed, overridden>>

Recall(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<licensed, round, tally, dispensed, overridden>>

\* A withdrawal empties the tally outright: ballots collected under the old
\* roll are no longer evidence of anything.  The roll may never be taken
\* below quorum size.
WithdrawLicence(p) ==
    /\ p \in licensed
    /\ Cardinality(licensed) - 1 >= Quorum
    /\ licensed' = licensed \ {p}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, dispensed, overridden>>

\* The duty manager's privileged path, which consults no ballots at all.
ManagerOverride(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed \union {s}
    /\ overridden' = overridden \union {s}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED licensed

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : CastBallot(p)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : Recall(s)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : WithdrawLicence(p)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : ManagerOverride(s)

VoteStep == \E p \in Pharmacists : CastBallot(p)

ClearStep == \E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(VoteStep)
    /\ WF_Vars(ClearStep)

\* Authorisation: nothing unlicensed and nothing stale is sitting in the
\* live tally that the cabinet counts against quorum.
TallyIsCurrentAndLicensed ==
    \A b \in tally : b.ph \in licensed /\ b.rnd = round

\* Progress: the queue does not stall short of quorum forever.
QueueEventuallyClears == <>(queue = {})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Pharmacists = {phDunn, phIyer, phKoch}
    Scripts = {rxOne, rxTwo}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxRound = 4

INVARIANT TallyIsCurrentAndLicensed
PROPERTY QueueEventuallyClears

\* An empty queue with the roll settled is the end of the shift, not a
\* deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy dispenses controlled prescriptions through a cabinet that will not open on one person's say-so. Each prescription waiting in the queue needs a quorum of approvals from pharmacists who currently hold a valid dispensing licence. Approvals are collected in rounds: the cabinet keeps a live tally of ballots, and every ballot carries the round it was cast in.

A licensed pharmacist who has not already voted in the current round may cast a ballot into the live tally. When the tally holds at least a quorum of ballots, any queued prescription may be dispensed: it leaves the queue, it is added to the dispensed record, the live tally is emptied, and the round advances. A prescription can also simply be recalled from the queue -- the patient cancelled -- which dispenses nothing and does not disturb the tally.

Licences can be withdrawn. When a pharmacist's licence is withdrawn, that pharmacist comes off the licensed roll, the round advances, and the live tally is emptied outright, because ballots collected under the old roll are no longer evidence of anything. The pharmacy is never allowed to withdraw a licence that would take the licensed roll below quorum size.

The duty manager holds a privileged override. The manager can dispense a queued prescription with no quorum at all -- the prescription leaves the queue, goes into the dispensed record and is additionally flagged in the override register, the tally is emptied and the round advances. The override is the one path that does not consult the ballots.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every ballot sitting in the cabinet's live tally belongs to a pharmacist who is still on the licensed roll and was cast in the round that is currently open.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The prescription queue is eventually emptied -- every queued prescription is eventually dispensed, overridden or recalled.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, GridCap, LocalLimit, MaxStamp, NoToken

Stations == 0..(RingSize - 1)

Downstream(s) == (s + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES load, held, inbox, stamp, shedTally

Vars == <<load, held, inbox, stamp, shedTally>>

\* A token carries the headroom that was measured when it was minted, so an
\* out-of-date token would hand out an allowance the grid no longer has.
Token == [st: 0..MaxStamp, allow: 0..GridCap]

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Connected == Tally(load, Stations)

Headroom == IF Connected >= GridCap THEN 0 ELSE GridCap - Connected

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Stations -> 0..LocalLimit]
    /\ held \in [Stations -> {NoToken} \union Token]
    /\ inbox \in [Stations -> {NoToken} \union Token]
    /\ stamp \in 0..MaxStamp
    /\ shedTally \in Nat

Init ==
    /\ load = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ held = [s \in Stations |-> IF s = 0 THEN [st |-> 0, allow |-> GridCap]
                                  ELSE NoToken]
    /\ inbox = [s \in Stations |-> NoToken]
    /\ stamp = 0
    /\ shedTally = 0

\* Reconnecting burns allowance off the token, not off a fresh reading.
Reconnect(s) ==
    /\ held[s] # NoToken
    /\ held[s].allow > 0
    /\ load[s] < LocalLimit
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s].allow = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, stamp, shedTally>>

PassToken(s) ==
    /\ held[s] # NoToken
    /\ inbox[Downstream(s)] = NoToken
    /\ stamp < MaxStamp
    /\ inbox' = [inbox EXCEPT ![Downstream(s)] = [st |-> stamp + 1,
                                                 allow |-> Headroom]]
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = NoToken]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, shedTally>>

\* The stamp test is the only thing separating a token that is genuinely
\* current from one that has been overtaken in the network.
Install(s) ==
    /\ inbox[s] # NoToken
    /\ inbox[s].st = stamp
    /\ held[s] = NoToken
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = inbox[s]]
    /\ inbox' = [inbox EXCEPT ![s] = NoToken]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, stamp, shedTally>>

DropOvertaken(s) ==
    /\ inbox[s] # NoToken
    /\ inbox[s].st # stamp
    /\ inbox' = [inbox EXCEPT ![s] = NoToken]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, held, stamp, shedTally>>

\* With nobody holding a token the controller assumes it was lost and mints
\* a replacement -- which is how two tokens come to be alive at once.
MintReplacement(s) ==
    /\ \A t \in Stations : held[t] = NoToken
    /\ inbox[s] = NoToken
    /\ stamp < MaxStamp
    /\ inbox' = [inbox EXCEPT ![s] = [st |-> stamp + 1, allow |-> Headroom]]
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, held, shedTally>>

ShedFeeder(s) ==
    /\ load[s] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
    /\ shedTally' = shedTally + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, inbox, stamp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Reconnect(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : PassToken(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Install(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : DropOvertaken(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : MintReplacement(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : ShedFeeder(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Shedding is the only unbounded dimension of the model, so capping the
\* tally is what keeps it finite.
ShedBound == shedTally <= GridCap

\* Bounded capacity: connected load never exceeds rated headroom, however
\* tokens are overtaken or replaced in the ring network.
HeadroomNeverExceeded == Connected <= GridCap
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    GridCap = 2
    LocalLimit = 2
    MaxStamp = 4
    NoToken = notoken

CONSTRAINT ShedBound

INVARIANT HeadroomNeverExceeded

\* Once the stamp budget is spent and nothing is in flight the ring is
\* quiescent, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional power grid runs a load shedder across a ring of substations. Generation headroom is finite: the total load connected across the whole ring must never exceed the grid's rated headroom. Authorisation to reconnect feeders circulates as a ring token. A token is not just a permission -- it carries a connect allowance, which is the headroom the controller measured at the moment the token was minted, and it carries the ring's current token stamp.

A substation holding a token may reconnect one feeder if its allowance is not yet spent and its own feeder count is below its local limit; doing so burns one unit of allowance. A substation holding a token may instead pass it on: the token goes into the next substation's inbox along the ring, freshly stamped and carrying a freshly measured allowance, and the passing substation is left holding nothing.

The ring network does not preserve order, and inboxes are consumed independently, so a token that was launched earlier can still be sitting undelivered while a later one is already in use. A substation installs a token from its inbox only if the token's stamp is the ring's current stamp; the substation must not already be holding one. A token whose stamp is not current is dropped from the inbox unread.

If no substation anywhere on the ring is holding a token, the controller concludes the token was lost in the network and mints a replacement into some substation's inbox, freshly stamped and with a freshly measured allowance. This is the situation in which two tokens can be alive at once: the replacement and whatever was actually still in flight. Finally, any substation with load on it may shed one feeder, which decreases its load and adds to the shed tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total load connected across all substations on the ring never exceeds the grid's rated headroom.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Servers, Makers, Parties, PlayerCap, Horizon, LeaseSpan,
          NoMaker, NoServer, NoParty

\* A party's identifier is its headcount, so the queue is a set of headcounts.
ASSUME Parties \subseteq 1..PlayerCap

VARIABLES occupancy, leaseOwner, leaseEnd, clock, plan, status

Vars == <<occupancy, leaseOwner, leaseEnd, clock, plan, status>>

Queued == {p \in Parties : status[p] = "queued"}

Deadline == IF clock + LeaseSpan > Horizon THEN Horizon ELSE clock + LeaseSpan

SeatsLeft(s) == IF occupancy[s] >= PlayerCap THEN 0 ELSE PlayerCap - occupancy[s]

\* A lease is only good while its holder is still the recorded one and the
\* shared clock has not passed its deadline.
Live(m, s) == leaseOwner[s] = m /\ clock < leaseEnd[s]

Idle == [srv |-> NoServer, pty |-> NoParty, room |-> 0]

TypeOK ==
    /\ occupancy \in [Servers -> 0..(2 * PlayerCap)]
    /\ leaseOwner \in [Servers -> {NoMaker} \union Makers]
    /\ leaseEnd \in [Servers -> 0..Horizon] /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ plan \in [Makers -> [srv: {NoServer} \union Servers,
                 pty: {NoParty} \union Parties, room: 0..(2 * PlayerCap)]]
    /\ status \in [Parties -> {"queued", "assigned", "seated", "bounced"}]

Init ==
    /\ occupancy = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ leaseOwner = [s \in Servers |-> NoMaker]
    /\ leaseEnd = [s \in Servers |-> 0] /\ clock = 0
    /\ plan = [m \in Makers |-> Idle]
    /\ status = [p \in Parties |-> "queued"]

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, leaseOwner, leaseEnd, plan, status>>

TakeLease(m, s) ==
    /\ plan[m].srv = NoServer
    /\ (leaseOwner[s] = NoMaker \/ clock >= leaseEnd[s])
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![s] = m]
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![s] = Deadline]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![m] = [srv |-> s, pty |-> NoParty, room |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, clock, status>>

\* The seat figure is measured here, once, and is never refreshed.
AssignParty(m, p) ==
    /\ plan[m].srv # NoServer /\ plan[m].pty = NoParty /\ status[p] = "queued"
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![m] = [srv |-> plan[m].srv, pty |-> p,
                                    room |-> SeatsLeft(plan[m].srv)]]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "assigned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, leaseOwner, leaseEnd, clock>>

Seat(m) ==
    /\ plan[m].pty # NoParty /\ Live(m, plan[m].srv)
    /\ plan[m].pty <= plan[m].room
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![plan[m].srv] = @ + plan[m].pty]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![plan[m].pty] = "seated"]
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![plan[m].srv] = NoMaker]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![m] = Idle] /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseEnd, clock>>

Bounce(m) ==
    /\ plan[m].pty # NoParty /\ Live(m, plan[m].srv)
    /\ plan[m].pty > plan[m].room
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![plan[m].pty] = "bounced"]
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![plan[m].srv] = NoMaker]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![m] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, leaseEnd, clock>>

\* The lease is no longer ours, so we do not hand it back -- somebody else
\* may already be holding it.
StandDown(m) ==
    /\ plan[m].srv # NoServer /\ ~Live(m, plan[m].srv)
    /\ status' = IF plan[m].pty = NoParty THEN status
                 ELSE [status EXCEPT ![plan[m].pty] = "bounced"]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![m] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, leaseOwner, leaseEnd, clock>>

MatchEnds(s) ==
    /\ occupancy[s] > 0 /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseEnd, clock, plan, status>>

MatchStep ==
    \E m \in Makers : \/ \E s \in Servers : TakeLease(m, s)
                      \/ \E p \in Parties : AssignParty(m, p)
                      \/ Seat(m) \/ Bounce(m) \/ StandDown(m)

Next == MatchStep \/ Tick \/ (\E s \in Servers : MatchEnds(s))

AssignStep == \E m \in Makers, p \in Parties : AssignParty(m, p)

\* A lease taken at the very end of the horizon is dead on arrival, so the
\* two instances can churn leases indefinitely; strong fairness on assignment
\* is what stops a party being passed over forever inside that churn.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(MatchStep) /\ SF_Vars(AssignStep)

\* Bounded capacity: a server is never seated past its cap, however leases
\* lapse between measuring the seats and filling them.
CapNeverExceeded == \A s \in Servers : occupancy[s] <= PlayerCap

\* Progress: waiting parties do not sit in the queue forever.
QueueDrains == (Queued # {}) ~> (Queued = {})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Servers = {srvEast, srvWest}
    Makers = {mmAlpha, mmBeta}
    Parties = {1, 2}
    PlayerCap = 2
    Horizon = 3
    LeaseSpan = 2
    NoMaker = nomaker
    NoServer = noserver
    NoParty = noparty

INVARIANT CapNeverExceeded
PROPERTY QueueDrains
nl:
A multiplayer game runs two independently deployed matchmaker instances that draw on one shared pool of game servers. The instances were stood up separately in different regions and never talk to each other. Each game server has a hard player cap and must never be seated beyond it, because an over-seated server drops everybody in it.

Access to a server is regulated by a time-bounded lease. There is a shared wall clock that only ever advances. A matchmaker instance with no work in hand may take the lease on a server whose lease is unheld or whose lease deadline has already passed; the lease is stamped with a deadline a fixed span into the future, never past the end of the horizon. Taking the lease is all the instance does at that point -- it has a server but no party.

Parties wait in a queue, each with a fixed headcount. An instance holding a server lease may assign one queued party to itself; at that moment, and only at that moment, it measures the seats remaining on that server. The party is off the queue from then on and never goes back on it.

To seat the party, the instance must still be the recorded lease holder and the clock must still be inside its lease deadline, and the party's headcount must fit the seat figure it measured. Seating adds the headcount to the server's occupancy, marks the party seated, and hands the lease back. If the party does not fit the measured figure, the instance bounces the party instead, also handing the lease back. An instance that finds it is no longer the recorded holder, or that its deadline has passed, stands down: it drops whatever it was holding, bouncing any party it had assigned, and does not touch the lease because the lease is no longer its to release. Separately, the clock may tick forward, and any occupied server's match may end, which empties that server.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No game server's occupancy ever exceeds its player cap, even when a lease deadline passes between the moment an instance measured the remaining seats and the moment it tries to seat its party.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever parties are waiting, the queue is eventually cleared -- every waiting party is eventually either seated or bounced.

---- MODULE W4Od14m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, RingSize, Budget, NoDrone

Stations == 0..(RingSize - 1)

Onward(s) == (s + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES alloc, reserve, tokenAt, draft, flown

Vars == <<alloc, reserve, tokenAt, draft, flown>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Allocated == Tally(alloc, Drones)

Blank == [drn |-> NoDrone, hours |-> 0, resRead |-> 0]

TypeOK ==
    /\ alloc \in [Drones -> 0..Budget] /\ reserve \in 0..Budget
    /\ tokenAt \in Stations /\ flown \in 0..Budget
    /\ draft \in [Stations -> [drn: {NoDrone} \union Drones,
                  hours: 0..Budget, resRead: 0..Budget]]

Init ==
    /\ alloc = [d \in Drones |-> 0] /\ reserve = Budget
    /\ tokenAt = 0 /\ flown = 0
    /\ draft = [s \in Stations |-> Blank]

\* Handing the token on voids the passing station's draft: the reading it
\* was built on stops being trustworthy the moment the token leaves.
PassToken(s) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s /\ tokenAt' = Onward(s)
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, reserve, flown>>

\* Drafting reads the reserve once, under the token.
Draft(s, d, n) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s /\ draft[s].drn = NoDrone /\ n > 0
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = [drn |-> d, hours |-> n,
                                      resRead |-> reserve]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, reserve, tokenAt, flown>>

\* The reserve is written back from the old reading, so the token is the only
\* thing that makes that reading still true.
Commit(s) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s /\ draft[s].drn # NoDrone
    /\ draft[s].hours <= draft[s].resRead
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![draft[s].drn] = @ + draft[s].hours]
    /\ reserve' = draft[s].resRead - draft[s].hours
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, flown>>

Discard(s) ==
    /\ draft[s].drn # NoDrone
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, reserve, tokenAt, flown>>

FlyHour(d) ==
    /\ alloc[d] > 0 /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ flown' = flown + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve, tokenAt, draft>>

\* Handing an hour back also amends the reserve, so it too needs the token,
\* and it must not race the station's own outstanding draft.
ReturnHour(s, d) ==
    /\ tokenAt = s /\ draft[s].drn = NoDrone /\ alloc[d] > 0
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, draft, flown>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Stations : PassToken(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations, d \in Drones, n \in 1..Budget : Draft(s, d, n)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Commit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Discard(s)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : FlyHour(d)
    \/ \E s \in Stations, d \in Drones : ReturnHour(s, d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: allocated plus reserved plus flown is always exactly the
\* incident budget, so no ledger amendment mints or loses an hour.
HoursConserved == Allocated + reserve + flown = Budget
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drScout, drThermal}
    RingSize = 2
    Budget = 3
    NoDrone = nodrone

INVARIANT HoursConserved
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm is flown from two independently deployed ground-station instances that share one pool of drones. The two instances were set up by different incident teams and never talk to each other directly. The swarm's whole operating budget is a fixed number of flight hours for the incident, and every hour is accounted for: an hour is either allocated to a particular drone, sitting unallocated in the reserve, or already flown. Hours may not be invented and may not go missing.

The right to amend the hour ledger circulates around the two stations as a ring token, and only the station currently holding the token may amend it. A station holding the token may hand it on around the ring at any time; handing it on voids whatever draft that station had outstanding, because the reading the draft was built on stops being trustworthy the moment the token leaves.

A station holding the token drafts an amendment: it names a drone, names how many hours it wants to give that drone, and writes down the reserve figure it read at that moment. A station may only hold one draft at a time. To commit, the station must still hold the token, and the hours it wants must not exceed the reserve figure it wrote down; committing adds the hours to that drone's allocation and writes the reserve back as the figure it wrote down minus the hours it took -- an absolute value derived from the old reading, not a subtraction applied to the current reserve. A station may also simply discard an outstanding draft of its own.

Two other things happen to hours. Any drone with allocated hours may fly one of them, which moves that hour out of the drone's allocation and into the flown tally. And a station holding the token, with no draft of its own outstanding, may take one allocated hour back off a drone and return it to the reserve.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The hours allocated across all drones, plus the hours sitting in the reserve, plus the hours already flown always add up to exactly the incident's flight-hour budget.

---- MODULE W4Od3m1p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, Batches, Face, NoBatch

Banks == 0..(RingSize - 1)

Onward(k) == (k + 1) % RingSize

Funding == Cardinality(Batches) * Face

VARIABLES register, debited, tokenAt, inHand, reserve, overrides

Vars == <<register, debited, tokenAt, inHand, reserve, overrides>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ register \in [Batches -> {"open", "claimed", "settled"}]
    /\ debited \in [Batches -> 0..(2 * Face)]
    /\ tokenAt \in Banks /\ reserve \in 0..Funding
    /\ inHand \in [Banks -> {NoBatch} \union Batches]
    /\ overrides \subseteq Batches

Init ==
    /\ register = [b \in Batches |-> "open"]
    /\ debited = [b \in Batches |-> 0]
    /\ tokenAt = 0 /\ reserve = Funding
    /\ inHand = [k \in Banks |-> NoBatch]
    /\ overrides = {}

PassToken(k) ==
    /\ tokenAt = k /\ tokenAt' = Onward(k)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, debited, inHand, reserve, overrides>>

Claim(k, b) ==
    /\ tokenAt = k /\ inHand[k] = NoBatch /\ register[b] = "open"
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![b] = "claimed"]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![k] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<debited, tokenAt, reserve, overrides>>

\* The token is what earns a bank its claim; once claimed, the batch is that
\* bank's to settle even after the token has moved on around the ring.
Settle(k) ==
    /\ inHand[k] # NoBatch
    /\ register[inHand[k]] = "claimed" /\ reserve >= Face
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![inHand[k]] = "settled"]
    /\ debited' = [debited EXCEPT ![inHand[k]] = Face]
    /\ reserve' = reserve - Face
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![k] = NoBatch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, overrides>>

\* Letting go only reopens a batch that had got no further than claimed.
LetGo(k) ==
    /\ inHand[k] # NoBatch
    /\ register' = IF register[inHand[k]] = "claimed"
                   THEN [register EXCEPT ![inHand[k]] = "open"] ELSE register
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![k] = NoBatch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<debited, tokenAt, reserve, overrides>>

\* The duty officer's privileged posting: no token, no claim required.
ForceSettle(b) ==
    /\ register[b] # "settled" /\ reserve >= Face
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![b] = "settled"]
    /\ debited' = [debited EXCEPT ![b] = Face]
    /\ reserve' = reserve - Face
    /\ overrides' = overrides \union {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, inHand>>

HandToken(k) ==
    /\ tokenAt # k /\ tokenAt' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, debited, inHand, reserve, overrides>>

ClaimStep == \E k \in Banks, b \in Batches : Claim(k, b)

SettleStep == \E k \in Banks : Settle(k)

RingStep ==
    \/ \E k \in Banks : PassToken(k)
    \/ ClaimStep \/ SettleStep \/ (\E k \in Banks : LetGo(k))

Next ==
    \/ RingStep
    \/ \E b \in Batches : ForceSettle(b)
    \/ \E k \in Banks : HandToken(k)

\* The token can be passed round the ring forever, so weak fairness alone
\* would let a batch be walked past indefinitely; the claim and settle steps
\* need strong fairness to get a foot in that cycle.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(RingStep) /\ SF_Vars(ClaimStep) /\ SF_Vars(SettleStep)

\* Irreversibility: the debit recorded against a batch is its face value once
\* it is stamped settled and nothing before that, so no batch is paid twice.
DebitedExactlyOnce ==
    \A b \in Batches :
        debited[b] = IF register[b] = "settled" THEN Face ELSE 0

\* Progress: the day's batches all reach settlement.
AllBatchesSettle == <>(\A b \in Batches : register[b] = "settled")
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Batches = {btGilt, btRepo}
    Face = 1
    NoBatch = nobatch

INVARIANT DebitedExactlyOnce
PROPERTY AllBatchesSettle
nl:
A clearing house settles a set of interbank batches at the end of each day. Settling a batch is final: the money leaves the clearing reserve, the batch is stamped settled on the central register, and there is no mechanism anywhere in the system to unstamp it or to claw the money back. A batch must therefore be settled at most once -- settling the same batch twice would take its face value out of the reserve twice with no way to undo either debit.

The right to post to the central register circulates among the member banks as a ring token. A bank holding the token may hand it on to the next bank around the ring at any time. A bank holding the token, with no batch of its own in hand, may claim a batch that is still open on the register; claiming marks the batch claimed and puts it in that bank's hands. The token is what earns a bank its claim; once a batch is in a bank's hands it is that bank's to settle even after the token has moved on around the ring. To settle, the batch in the bank's hands must still be marked claimed: settling debits the batch's face value from the clearing reserve, records that debit against the batch, stamps the batch settled and empties the bank's hands. A bank may also let go of whatever batch it has in hand at any time, which returns the batch to open if it was still merely claimed and otherwise leaves the register alone.

The clearing house's duty officer holds two privileged powers that do not respect the ring. The officer can force-settle any batch that is not yet stamped settled, without holding the token and without the batch having been claimed: the debit is taken, the batch is stamped settled, and the batch is noted in the override register. The officer can also hand the token directly to any member bank, out of ring order.

The clearing reserve is funded at exactly the total face value of the day's batches.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every batch, the amount recorded as debited against it is its face value if the batch is stamped settled and zero otherwise, so no batch is ever debited twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch in the day's set is eventually stamped settled.

---- MODULE W4Od19m9p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Shelves, Instances, MaxCap, MaxEpoch, NoShelf

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, holds, prep, turnedAway

Vars == <<epoch, capacity, holds, prep, turnedAway>>

Configs == [Shelves -> 0..MaxCap]

Blank == [shf |-> NoShelf, ep |-> 0, room |-> 0]

\* The epoch belongs to the shared shelf register as a whole: every write to
\* it advances the epoch, and republishing a configuration is one such write.
\* Room is worked out once, under the register as it stood at that moment.
Room(s) == IF holds[s] >= capacity[s] THEN 0 ELSE capacity[s] - holds[s]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ capacity \in Configs
    /\ holds \in [Shelves -> 0..(2 * MaxCap)]
    /\ prep \in [Instances -> [shf: {NoShelf} \union Shelves,
                 ep: 0..MaxEpoch, room: 0..MaxCap]]
    /\ turnedAway \subseteq Instances

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0 /\ capacity = [s \in Shelves |-> MaxCap]
    /\ holds = [s \in Shelves |-> 0]
    /\ prep = [i \in Instances |-> Blank]
    /\ turnedAway = {}

\* A new configuration may not shrink a shelf below what is already on it,
\* so publishing one can never break the capacity rule by itself.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \A s \in Shelves : c[s] >= holds[s]
    /\ capacity' = c /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, prep, turnedAway>>

Prepare(i, s) ==
    /\ prep[i].shf = NoShelf
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![i] = [shf |-> s, ep |-> epoch, room |-> Room(s)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, holds, turnedAway>>

\* The books go on against the old room figure, so the epoch test is the only
\* thing tying that figure to the configuration actually in force.
Place(i) ==
    /\ prep[i].shf # NoShelf /\ prep[i].ep = epoch /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![prep[i].shf] = @ + prep[i].room]
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![i] = Blank]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, turnedAway>>

Abandon(i) ==
    /\ prep[i].shf # NoShelf /\ prep[i].ep # epoch
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![i] = Blank]
    /\ turnedAway' = turnedAway \union {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, holds>>

Collect(s) ==
    /\ holds[s] > 0 /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1] /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, prep, turnedAway>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Configs : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Shelves : Prepare(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Place(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Abandon(i)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : Collect(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Bounded capacity: no shelf carries more than the configuration in force
\* allows it to, however configurations are republished mid-preparation.
ShelvesWithinCapacity == \A s \in Shelves : holds[s] <= capacity[s]
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Shelves = {shMain, shAnnex}
    Instances = {rsvNorth, rsvSouth}
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxEpoch = 4
    NoShelf = noshelf

INVARIANT ShelvesWithinCapacity

\* With the epoch budget spent and no preparation outstanding the register is
\* quiescent, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A county library runs two independently deployed instances of its reservation service, and both draw on one shared pool of hold shelves. The instances were commissioned by different branch systems and never talk to each other. Each hold shelf has a configured capacity and must never carry more reserved books than that, because an over-stuffed shelf spills and books get mis-filed.

The shared shelf register carries an epoch number, and every write to that register advances it -- putting books on a shelf, taking a book off a shelf, and republishing the shelving configuration are all writes to it. Shelf capacities are set by that shelving configuration. Facilities may publish a new configuration at any time; a new configuration may never set a shelf's capacity below the number of books already sitting on that shelf, so publishing one is always safe in itself.

An instance places reservations in two steps. First it prepares: it picks a shelf, writes down the epoch of the configuration it read, and works out how many books that shelf could still take under that configuration. Then it places: it puts that many reserved books onto the shelf in one go, advancing the epoch, and finishes its work. Placing is only allowed if the epoch it wrote down is still the current epoch. An instance whose epoch has been superseded abandons its preparation and is noted as having been turned away; it does not place anything.

Separately, a patron may collect one reserved book from any shelf that has something on it, which takes that book off the shelf and also advances the epoch.

The important detail is that the room figure an instance places against is the figure it worked out at preparation time, under the configuration that was current then -- it is never recomputed against the configuration in force when the books actually go on the shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No hold shelf ever carries more reserved books than the capacity set for it by the configuration currently in force.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m2p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Parts, Leg, Opening, MaxRound

Total == Cardinality(Parts) * Opening

Notice == [to: Parts, kind: {"commit", "abort"}, rnd: 0..MaxRound]

VARIABLES balance, vote, round, decision, notices, settled

Vars == <<balance, vote, round, decision, notices, settled>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

\* A participant that has voted yes is holding its leg out of its balance;
\* that earmarked money is part of the batch's accounting, not lost.
Earmarked == Cardinality({p \in Parts : vote[p] = "yes"}) * Leg

TypeOK ==
    /\ balance \in [Parts -> 0..(2 * Total)] /\ settled \in 0..Total
    /\ vote \in [Parts -> {"none", "yes", "no", "applied"}]
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ decision \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}
    /\ notices \subseteq Notice

Init ==
    /\ balance = [p \in Parts |-> Opening] /\ settled = 0
    /\ vote = [p \in Parts |-> "none"]
    /\ round = 0 /\ decision = "none" /\ notices = {}

EarmarkAndVoteYes(p) ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ vote[p] = "none" /\ balance[p] >= Leg
    /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![p] = @ - Leg]
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, decision, notices, settled>>

VoteNo(p) ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ vote[p] = "none" /\ balance[p] < Leg
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, round, decision, notices, settled>>

Decide ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ \A p \in Parts : vote[p] \in {"yes", "no"}
    /\ decision' = IF \A p \in Parts : vote[p] = "yes" THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
    /\ notices' = notices \union
         {[to |-> p, kind |-> decision', rnd |-> round] : p \in Parts}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, vote, round, settled>>

\* The coordinator re-issues notices it has had no answer to, so an inbox can
\* hold a notice the participant already acted on.
Reissue(p) ==
    /\ decision # "none"
    /\ notices' = notices \union {[to |-> p, kind |-> decision, rnd |-> round]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, vote, round, decision, settled>>

ApplyCommit(m) ==
    /\ m \in notices /\ m.kind = "commit" /\ m.rnd = round
    /\ vote[m.to] = "yes"
    /\ settled' = settled + Leg
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![m.to] = "applied"]
    /\ notices' = notices \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, round, decision>>

ApplyAbort(m) ==
    /\ m \in notices /\ m.kind = "abort" /\ m.rnd = round
    /\ vote[m.to] = "yes"
    /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![m.to] = @ + Leg]
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![m.to] = "applied"]
    /\ notices' = notices \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, decision, settled>>

DiscardStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in notices /\ m.rnd # round
    /\ notices' = notices \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, vote, round, decision, settled>>

\* Leftover notices are deliberately not swept when a fresh round opens.
OpenRound ==
    /\ decision # "none" /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ \A p \in Parts : vote[p] # "yes"
    /\ round' = round + 1 /\ decision' = "none"
    /\ vote' = [p \in Parts |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, notices, settled>>

VoteStep == \E p \in Parts : EarmarkAndVoteYes(p) \/ VoteNo(p)

ApplyStep == \E m \in Notice : ApplyCommit(m) \/ ApplyAbort(m)

Next ==
    \/ VoteStep \/ Decide \/ ApplyStep \/ OpenRound
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Reissue(p)
    \/ \E m \in Notice : DiscardStale(m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(VoteStep) /\ WF_Vars(Decide) /\ WF_Vars(ApplyStep)

\* Conservation: balances plus earmarked legs plus settled money is always
\* exactly the opening sum, so no notice ever mints or loses a leg.
FundsConserved == Tally(balance, Parts) + Earmarked + settled = Total

\* Progress: the batch really does settle in full.

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Parts = {bkNordia, bkSudbank}
    Leg = 1
    Opening = 3
    MaxRound = 3

INVARIANT FundsConserved
PROPERTY BatchFullySettled

\* A closed-out batch with the round budget spent is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A clearing house settles a batch across two participant banks using a two-phase commit. Every unit of money in the batch is accounted for at all times: it is either sitting in a participant's own balance, earmarked by a participant that has voted to commit, or already settled into the batch total. Money is never minted and never lost.

Phase one is the vote. While no decision has been reached, a participant that has not yet voted either earmarks the leg amount out of its own balance and votes yes, or -- if its balance will not cover the leg -- votes no without moving anything. Once every participant has voted, the coordinator decides: commit if every vote was yes, abort otherwise. Deciding also puts one decision notice for each participant onto the network, stamped with the round the decision belongs to and naming the leg amount.

Phase two is the apply. The network does not preserve order and the coordinator may re-issue a decision notice to any participant at any time while a decision stands, so a participant's inbox can hold notices it has already acted on and notices belonging to a round that has since been closed. A participant applies a commit notice by moving its earmarked leg into the batch total; it applies an abort notice by returning its earmarked leg to its own balance. Either way the participant is then marked as having applied. A participant may only act on a notice if it currently has a leg earmarked and if the notice's round stamp is the round now open; notices whose round stamp is stale may be discarded unread.

When a decision stands and no participant still has a leg earmarked, the coordinator may open a fresh round: the round number advances, the decision is cleared, and every participant goes back to not having voted. Notices left over on the network are not swept up when this happens.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The money sitting in participants' balances, plus the legs currently earmarked, plus the money already settled into the batch total always add up to exactly the amount the batch started with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The batch total eventually reaches the full sum of all participants' legs.
