---- MODULE W4Od9m4p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, Commands, QueueCap, MaxGen, NoWorker

Grant == [to: Workers, gen: 0..MaxGen]

VARIABLES holder, phase, cmdState, bus, gen

Vars == <<holder, phase, cmdState, bus, gen>>

Queued == {c \in Commands : cmdState[c] = "queued"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in {NoWorker} \union Workers /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ phase \in [Workers -> {"idle", "waiting", "driving"}]
    /\ cmdState \in [Commands -> {"new", "queued", "refused", "done"}]
    /\ bus \subseteq Grant

Init ==
    /\ holder = NoWorker /\ gen = 0
    /\ phase = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]
    /\ cmdState = [c \in Commands |-> "new"]
    /\ bus = {}

\* Backpressure: a full queue refuses work rather than growing.
Admit(c) ==
    /\ cmdState[c] = "new" /\ Cardinality(Queued) < QueueCap
    /\ cmdState' = [cmdState EXCEPT ![c] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase, bus, gen>>

Refuse(c) ==
    /\ cmdState[c] = "new" /\ Cardinality(Queued) >= QueueCap
    /\ cmdState' = [cmdState EXCEPT ![c] = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase, bus, gen>>

\* Handing the interlock over advances the generation and records the holder
\* in the same step, which is what ties a grant stamp to a real holder.
HandOver(w) ==
    /\ holder = NoWorker /\ phase[w] = "idle" /\ Queued # {} /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1 /\ holder' = w
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "waiting"]
    /\ bus' = bus \union {[to |-> w, gen |-> gen + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED cmdState

\* Grants linger on the bus, so the stamp is the only evidence a grant is
\* still the live one.
PickUp(g) ==
    /\ g \in bus /\ g.gen = gen /\ phase[g.to] = "waiting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![g.to] = "driving"]
    /\ bus' = bus \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cmdState, gen>>

Execute(w, c) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "driving" /\ cmdState[c] = "queued" /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ cmdState' = [cmdState EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ holder' = NoWorker /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED bus

\* The timeout clears the holder record but leaves the worker waiting, still
\* expecting the grant it was promised.
TimeOut(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "waiting" /\ holder = w /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = NoWorker /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cmdState, bus>>

GiveUp(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "waiting" /\ holder # w
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cmdState, bus, gen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Commands : Admit(c) \/ Refuse(c)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : HandOver(w) \/ TimeOut(w) \/ GiveUp(w)
    \/ \E g \in Grant : PickUp(g)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, c \in Commands : Execute(w, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the actuator: whoever is driving it is the recorded
\* holder of the interlock, and the record names at most one worker.
OnlyHolderDrives == \A w \in Workers : phase[w] = "driving" => holder = w
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {shdA, shdB}
    Commands = {cmdFeeder1, cmdFeeder2, cmdFeeder3}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxGen = 4
    NoWorker = noworker

INVARIANT OnlyHolderDrives

\* With the generation budget spent and the queue worked off the shedder is
\* quiescent, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder takes shed commands into a bounded work queue and executes them against a single breaker actuator. The actuator is the critical resource: it is a physical linkage and exactly one shedding worker may be driving it at any instant, or the linkage jams.

The queue applies backpressure rather than growing. A new command is taken into the queue if the queue is below its cap; if the queue is already at its cap the command is refused outright and never runs.

Access to the actuator is arbitrated by an interlock. The interlock has a generation counter, and the record of who holds it. When the interlock is unheld and some worker is idle and there is queued work, the controller hands the interlock to that worker: the generation counter advances, the worker is recorded as the holder, the worker moves into waiting, and an interlock grant stamped with the new generation is put on the control bus.

The control bus does not preserve order, so grants can sit on it and be picked up long after they were issued. A waiting worker that picks up a grant stamped with the generation now current begins driving the actuator; the grant is consumed. A worker driving the actuator executes one queued command, marks it done, releases the interlock, advances the generation and goes back to idle.

Two things go wrong on purpose. The interlock times out on a worker that has been recorded as holder but has not started driving: the holder record is cleared and the generation advances, but the worker stays in waiting, still expecting the grant it was promised. And a worker in waiting that is no longer the recorded holder may give up and go back to idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any worker that is driving the breaker actuator is the worker currently recorded as holding the interlock, so two workers are never driving it at once.

---- MODULE W4Od17m9p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Bags, MaxEpoch, OnBelt, InChute

ASSUME OnBelt \notin Nodes /\ InChute \notin Nodes

VARIABLES epoch, inService, installed, bagAt, handRouted

Vars == <<epoch, inService, installed, bagAt, handRouted>>

Carrying(n) == {b \in Bags : bagAt[b] = n}

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ inService \subseteq Nodes
    /\ installed \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ bagAt \in [Bags -> Nodes \union {OnBelt, InChute}]
    /\ handRouted \subseteq Bags

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0 /\ inService = Nodes
    /\ installed = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ bagAt = [b \in Bags |-> OnBelt]
    /\ handRouted = {}

\* A republish may not orphan a bag, and it leaves every node running the
\* table it last installed.
Republish(cs) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ cs # {}
    /\ \A n \in Nodes \ cs : Carrying(n) = {}
    /\ inService' = cs /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<installed, bagAt, handRouted>>

\* Only in-service nodes are sent the new table; a node taken out of service
\* is cut out of the distribution and never learns of the change.
InstallTable(n) ==
    /\ installed[n] # epoch /\ n \in inService
    /\ installed' = [installed EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, bagAt, handRouted>>

\* A node acts on the strength of the table it installed; it does not consult
\* the in-service set.
TakeFromBelt(n, b) ==
    /\ bagAt[b] = OnBelt /\ installed[n] = epoch
    /\ bagAt' = [bagAt EXCEPT ![b] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, installed, handRouted>>

DivertToChute(n, b) ==
    /\ bagAt[b] = n /\ installed[n] = epoch
    /\ bagAt' = [bagAt EXCEPT ![b] = InChute]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, installed, handRouted>>

\* The supervisor's privileged path skips the sorting nodes altogether.
HandCarry(b) ==
    /\ bagAt[b] = OnBelt
    /\ bagAt' = [bagAt EXCEPT ![b] = InChute]
    /\ handRouted' = handRouted \union {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, installed>>

SortStep ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : InstallTable(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, b \in Bags : TakeFromBelt(n, b) \/ DivertToChute(n, b)

Next ==
    \/ SortStep
    \/ \E cs \in SUBSET Nodes : Republish(cs)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : HandCarry(b)

\* Republishing is bounded by the epoch budget, so weak fairness on the
\* sorting steps is enough to drain the belt once reconfiguration settles.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(SortStep)

\* Authorisation: no bag is ever left in the care of a node that the
\* configuration in force has taken out of service.
NoBagOnRetiredNode == \A b \in Bags : bagAt[b] \in Nodes => bagAt[b] \in inService

\* Progress: bags do not circulate forever.
AllBagsReachChute == <>(\A b \in Bags : bagAt[b] = InChute)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {sortP, sortQ, sortR}
    Bags = {bagRed, bagBlue}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    OnBelt = onbelt
    InChute = inchute

INVARIANT NoBagOnRetiredNode
PROPERTY AllBagsReachChute

\* A drained router with the epoch budget spent is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags from the induction belt, through a set of sorting nodes, into the make-up chute. Which sorting nodes are in service is decided by a routing configuration that carries an epoch number. Only a node that is in service under the configuration currently in force may have a bag on it -- a bag sitting on a node that has been taken out of service is a bag nobody is responsible for, and it goes round the loop until somebody notices.

Engineering may republish the routing configuration at any time, naming a new, non-empty set of in-service nodes; this advances the epoch. A republish is only permitted when no bag is sitting on any node that the new configuration takes out of service. Advancing the epoch leaves every node behind: each node is still running the table it last installed.

The new table is only distributed to nodes that are in service under it. A node whose installed epoch is behind the current one, and which is in service under the current configuration, installs the current table and catches up. A node that has been taken out of service is simply cut out of the distribution and never hears about the new configuration; from its own point of view it is still in service under the table it last installed.

A node whose installed epoch is the current epoch may take a bag off the induction belt onto itself, and a node whose installed epoch is the current epoch may divert a bag it is carrying into the make-up chute. Notice that neither of these actions consults the in-service set directly -- a node acts on the strength of the table it installed.

The duty supervisor has a privileged override: any bag still on the induction belt can be hand-carried straight into the make-up chute, bypassing the sorting nodes entirely, and is noted in the hand-routing log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag that is sitting on a sorting node is sitting on a node that is in service under the configuration currently in force.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag eventually reaches the make-up chute.

---- MODULE W4Od2m1p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS FleetSize, Aisles, MaxEpoch, NoRobot

Robots == 0..(FleetSize - 1)

Onward(r) == (r + 1) % FleetSize

VARIABLES tokenAt, ringEpoch, holdBy, holdEpoch, crashed, driven

Vars == <<tokenAt, ringEpoch, holdBy, holdEpoch, crashed, driven>>

Running(r) == r \notin crashed

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenAt \in Robots /\ ringEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ holdBy \in [Aisles -> {NoRobot} \union Robots]
    /\ holdEpoch \in [Aisles -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Robots /\ driven \subseteq Aisles

Init ==
    /\ tokenAt = 0 /\ ringEpoch = 0
    /\ holdBy = [a \in Aisles |-> NoRobot]
    /\ holdEpoch = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {} /\ driven = {}

PassToken(r) ==
    /\ tokenAt = r /\ Running(r) /\ tokenAt' = Onward(r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ringEpoch, holdBy, holdEpoch, crashed, driven>>

\* Only the token holder may write the board, and it stamps the epoch that
\* was current when it wrote.
Reserve(r, a) ==
    /\ tokenAt = r /\ Running(r) /\ holdBy[a] = NoRobot
    /\ holdBy' = [holdBy EXCEPT ![a] = r]
    /\ holdEpoch' = [holdEpoch EXCEPT ![a] = ringEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, ringEpoch, crashed, driven>>

DriveAisle(r, a) ==
    /\ holdBy[a] = r /\ Running(r) /\ holdEpoch[a] = ringEpoch
    /\ holdBy' = [holdBy EXCEPT ![a] = NoRobot]
    /\ driven' = driven \union {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, ringEpoch, holdEpoch, crashed>>

Abandon(r, a) ==
    /\ holdBy[a] = r /\ Running(r)
    /\ holdBy' = [holdBy EXCEPT ![a] = NoRobot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, ringEpoch, holdEpoch, crashed, driven>>

\* Silent: no hand-back, no release, no announcement.
Crash(r) ==
    /\ Running(r) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, ringEpoch, holdBy, holdEpoch, driven>>

\* Repair sweeps the whole board, not just the dead robot's reservations,
\* because after an epoch change no stamp on the board can be trusted.
Repair(r) ==
    /\ tokenAt \in crashed /\ Running(r) /\ ringEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ tokenAt' = r /\ ringEpoch' = ringEpoch + 1
    /\ holdBy' = [a \in Aisles |-> NoRobot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdEpoch, crashed, driven>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : PassToken(r) \/ Crash(r) \/ Repair(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles :
           Reserve(r, a) \/ DriveAisle(r, a) \/ Abandon(r, a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No stale participant holds the floor: every reservation standing on the
\* board carries the ring's current epoch.
NoStaleReservation ==
    \A a \in Aisles : holdBy[a] # NoRobot => holdEpoch[a] = ringEpoch
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    FleetSize = 3
    Aisles = {aisleA, aisleB}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoRobot = norobot

INVARIANT NoStaleReservation

\* A fleet that has crashed out with the epoch budget spent is stuck, which
\* is the outcome being modelled and not a deadlock to report.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse floor is worked by a fleet of picking robots that must not drive into an aisle another robot has reserved. Reservations are written to a shared aisle board, and the right to write to that board circulates as a ring token: only the robot currently holding the token may reserve an aisle.

The board also carries the ring's epoch. Every reservation on the board is stamped with the epoch that was current when it was made, and a reservation is only good while its stamp is the current epoch -- a stamp from an older epoch means the reservation was made by a robot that the ring has since given up on, and it is worthless.

A robot holding the token, and running, may hand the token on to the next robot around the ring, or reserve any aisle that is currently unreserved, stamping the reservation with the current epoch. A robot that holds a reservation stamped with the current epoch, and is running, may drive its aisle, which clears the reservation and records the aisle as driven. A running robot may also abandon a reservation of its own without driving it.

Any robot can crash silently. A crashed robot stops doing anything at all and nothing about the rest of the system changes: it does not hand back the token, it does not release its reservations, and no announcement is made. If the token is sitting on a crashed robot the ring is stuck, so the ring repairs itself: it advances the epoch, hands a fresh token to some running robot, and sweeps the board clear of every reservation, because after an epoch change no reservation on the board can be trusted -- including the ones belonging to robots that are still perfectly healthy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every reservation standing on the aisle board is stamped with the ring's current epoch, so no aisle is ever held by a stale reservation from a superseded epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m6p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Total, TankCap, Horizon, Span, NoDrone

Order == [drn: Drones, amt: 1..TankCap, resRead: 0..(2 * Total)]

VARIABLES reservoir, tank, dropped, lease, clock, air

Vars == <<reservoir, tank, dropped, lease, clock, air>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

\* One lease at a time, naming a drone and a deadline off the staging clock.
Live(d) == lease.drn = d /\ clock < lease.ends

OnAir(d) == \E o \in air : o.drn = d

TypeOK ==
    /\ reservoir \in 0..(2 * Total) /\ dropped \in 0..Total
    /\ tank \in [Drones -> 0..TankCap] /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ lease \in [drn: {NoDrone} \union Drones, ends: 0..(Horizon + Span)]
    /\ air \subseteq Order

Init ==
    /\ reservoir = Total /\ dropped = 0
    /\ tank = [d \in Drones |-> 0] /\ clock = 0
    /\ lease = [drn |-> NoDrone, ends |-> 0]
    /\ air = {}

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, tank, dropped, lease, air>>

TakeLease(d) ==
    /\ tank[d] < TankCap
    /\ (lease.drn = NoDrone \/ clock >= lease.ends)
    /\ lease' = [drn |-> d, ends |-> clock + Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, tank, dropped, clock, air>>

\* The order carries the reservoir level as the drone read it.
CutOrder(d, n) ==
    /\ Live(d) /\ ~OnAir(d)
    /\ n <= reservoir /\ tank[d] + n <= TankCap
    /\ air' = air \union {[drn |-> d, amt |-> n, resRead |-> reservoir]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, tank, dropped, lease, clock>>

\* The reservoir is written back from the old reading, so a live lease is the
\* only thing that makes that reading still true.
ApplyOrder(o) ==
    /\ o \in air /\ Live(o.drn)
    /\ reservoir' = o.resRead - o.amt
    /\ tank' = [tank EXCEPT ![o.drn] = @ + o.amt]
    /\ air' = air \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, lease, clock>>

DiscardOrder(o) ==
    /\ o \in air /\ ~Live(o.drn)
    /\ air' = air \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, tank, dropped, lease, clock>>

DropOnFire(d) ==
    /\ tank[d] > 0 /\ dropped < Total
    /\ tank' = [tank EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1] /\ dropped' = dropped + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, lease, clock, air>>

GrantStep == \E d \in Drones : TakeLease(d)

CutStep == \E d \in Drones, n \in 1..TankCap : CutOrder(d, n)

ApplyStep == \E o \in Order : ApplyOrder(o)

DropStep == \E d \in Drones : DropOnFire(d)

Next ==
    \/ Tick \/ GrantStep \/ CutStep \/ ApplyStep \/ DropStep
    \/ \E o \in Order : DiscardOrder(o)

\* Leases can be taken and expired forever at a fixed clock, so the cut and
\* apply steps need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(GrantStep) /\ WF_Vars(DropStep)
    /\ SF_Vars(CutStep) /\ SF_Vars(ApplyStep)

\* Conservation: reservoir plus tanks plus dropped is always exactly the
\* opening load, so no radio order mints or loses retardant.
RetardantConserved == reservoir + Tally(tank, Drones) + dropped = Total

\* Progress: the load really does end up on the fire.
AllRetardantDropped == <>(dropped = Total)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drAsh, drEmber}
    Total = 2
    TankCap = 1
    Horizon = 2
    Span = 2
    NoDrone = nodrone

INVARIANT RetardantConserved
PROPERTY AllRetardantDropped

\* An emptied reservoir with everything dropped is the end of the operation,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm carries fire retardant, refilling from a single mobile reservoir at the staging point. Every unit of retardant is accounted for: it is either in the reservoir, in some drone's tank, or already dropped on the fire. The dispatcher must never conjure retardant into existence or lose track of any.

The reservoir pump is held under a loading lease. There is one lease at a time, naming one drone and a deadline read off the staging clock, which only ever advances until the operation's horizon. A drone whose tank is not full may take the lease whenever the lease is unheld or the current lease's deadline has already passed; taking it gives that drone a fresh deadline a fixed span ahead of the clock as it stands.

Loading is done by radio order. A drone holding a live lease, with no order of its own already out on the air, cuts an order naming how much retardant it wants; the order carries the reservoir level the drone read at that moment, and the amount must fit both the reservoir as read and the space left in the drone's tank. Radio orders are not delivered in the order they were cut, so an order can be applied long after it left the drone.

Applying an order writes the reservoir level back as the level recorded on the order minus the amount taken -- an absolute figure derived from the old reading, not a subtraction from the reservoir as it now stands -- and adds the amount to the drone's tank. An order may only be applied if the drone that cut it is still the lease holder and its deadline has not yet passed. An order that fails that test is discarded off the air unread.

Two other things happen. The staging clock may tick forward while it is short of the horizon. And any drone with retardant in its tank may drop one unit on the fire, which moves that unit out of the tank and into the dropped tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The retardant in the reservoir, plus the retardant in all the drones' tanks, plus the retardant already dropped always adds up to exactly the amount the operation started with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The whole of the operation's retardant is eventually dropped on the fire.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m0p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, Boxes, Planners, MaxVer, RetryBudget, NoBox, NoSlot

VARIABLES standing, given, ver, attempt, retries

Vars == <<standing, given, ver, attempt, retries>>

Clear == [box |-> NoBox, slt |-> NoSlot, sawVer |-> 0]

Busy(p) == attempt[p].box # NoBox

TypeOK ==
    /\ standing \in [Slots -> {NoBox} \union Boxes]
    /\ given \in [Boxes -> {NoSlot} \union Slots]
    /\ ver \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ attempt \in [Planners -> [box: {NoBox} \union Boxes,
                    slt: {NoSlot} \union Slots, sawVer: 0..MaxVer]]
    /\ retries \in [Planners -> 0..RetryBudget]

Init ==
    /\ standing = [s \in Slots |-> NoBox]
    /\ given = [b \in Boxes |-> NoSlot]
    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ attempt = [p \in Planners |-> Clear]
    /\ retries = [p \in Planners |-> 0]

\* Optimistic: the planner takes a version reading and walks away with it.
Begin(p, b, s) ==
    /\ ~Busy(p) /\ given[b] = NoSlot /\ standing[s] = NoBox
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![p] = [box |-> b, slt |-> s,
                                          sawVer |-> ver[s]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, given, ver, retries>>

\* The version comparison is the whole of the check: the commit never looks
\* again at whether the slot still records itself empty.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ Busy(p) /\ attempt[p].sawVer = ver[attempt[p].slt]
    /\ ver[attempt[p].slt] < MaxVer
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![attempt[p].slt] = attempt[p].box]
    /\ given' = [given EXCEPT ![attempt[p].box] = attempt[p].slt]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![attempt[p].slt] = @ + 1]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![p] = Clear]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

Retry(p) ==
    /\ Busy(p) /\ attempt[p].sawVer # ver[attempt[p].slt]
    /\ retries[p] < RetryBudget
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![p] = Clear]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, given, ver>>

Abandon(p) ==
    /\ Busy(p) /\ attempt[p].sawVer # ver[attempt[p].slt]
    /\ retries[p] = RetryBudget
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![p] = Clear]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, given, ver, retries>>

Lift(b) ==
    /\ given[b] # NoSlot /\ ver[given[b]] < MaxVer
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![given[b]] = NoBox]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![given[b]] = @ + 1]
    /\ given' = [given EXCEPT ![b] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Planners, b \in Boxes, s \in Slots : Begin(p, b, s)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : Commit(p) \/ Retry(p) \/ Abandon(p)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Lift(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No double allocation: the two records agree, so a slot never ends up
\* recorded against one box while another box has been given that slot.

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Slots = {slotB2, slotB3}
    Boxes = {bxMaersk, bxEvergreen}
    Planners = {plnHarbour, plnQuay}
    MaxVer = 3
    RetryBudget = 1
    NoBox = nobox
    NoSlot = noslot

INVARIANT RecordsAgree

\* With every slot's version budget spent the yard is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs two independently deployed planner instances over one shared pool of stacking slots. They were commissioned by different terminal operators and never coordinate with each other. Two records describe where things are: each slot records which container is standing in it, and each container records which slot it has been given. The two records must agree -- a container that has been given a slot must be the container that slot says is standing in it, or the crane will be sent to put a box down on top of another box.

There is no lock over the slots. Instead every slot carries a version number, and a planner works optimistically. It begins an assignment by picking a container that has not been given a slot and a slot that records itself as empty, and writing down that slot's version number as it stood at that moment. Each planner instance has one assignment in progress at a time and a fixed retry budget for the shift.

To commit, the planner requires only that the slot's version number is still the number it wrote down. If it is, the planner writes the container into the slot's record and the slot into the container's record, and advances the slot's version. Notice that the commit does not re-check whether the slot still records itself as empty; the version comparison is the whole of the check.

If the version has moved on, the planner's reading is out of date. With retry budget left it burns one retry and drops the assignment for another attempt later; with the budget exhausted it drops the assignment for the shift. Separately, a container that has been given a slot may be lifted out: the slot's record goes back to empty, the container's record goes back to unassigned, and the slot's version advances.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every container that has been given a slot, that slot records that same container as the one standing in it, so no slot is ever allocated to two containers at once.

---- MODULE W4Od6m9p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, MaxEpoch, NoCar

VARIABLES inShaft, epoch, holder, permit, eligible, ran

Vars == <<inShaft, epoch, holder, permit, eligible, ran>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ inShaft \subseteq Cars /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ holder \in {NoCar} \union Cars
    /\ permit \in [Cars -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ eligible \subseteq Cars /\ ran \subseteq Cars

Init ==
    /\ inShaft = {} /\ epoch = 0 /\ holder = NoCar
    /\ permit = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ eligible = Cars /\ ran = {}

\* Republishing the dispatch configuration is only allowed with the hoistway
\* empty, but it does not reach a car that is already on its way to the door.
Republish(es) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ es # {} /\ inShaft = {}
    /\ eligible' = es /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inShaft, holder, permit, ran>>

IssuePermit(c) ==
    /\ holder = NoCar /\ c \in eligible /\ c \notin ran /\ c \notin inShaft
    /\ holder' = c
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inShaft, epoch, eligible, ran>>

\* Both tests matter: a dawdling car can turn up still recorded as holder but
\* with a superseded stamp, or with a good stamp after being de-recorded.
Enter(c) ==
    /\ holder = c /\ permit[c] = epoch /\ c \notin inShaft
    /\ inShaft' = inShaft \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, permit, eligible, ran>>

CompleteRun(c) ==
    /\ c \in inShaft
    /\ inShaft' = inShaft \ {c} /\ holder' = NoCar
    /\ ran' = ran \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, permit, eligible>>

\* Withdrawal is silent: the car is slow, not gone, and is not told.
Withdraw(c) ==
    /\ holder = c /\ c \notin inShaft /\ holder' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inShaft, epoch, permit, eligible, ran>>

BankStep ==
    \E c \in Cars : IssuePermit(c) \/ Enter(c) \/ CompleteRun(c)

EnterStep == \E c \in Cars : Enter(c)

WithdrawStep == \E c \in Cars : Withdraw(c)

Next ==
    \/ BankStep
    \/ \E es \in SUBSET Cars : Republish(es)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Withdraw(c)

\* The bank does not leave a permit outstanding forever, so withdrawal is
\* weakly fair; and since permits can be issued and withdrawn indefinitely,
\* the entry step needs strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(BankStep) /\ WF_Vars(WithdrawStep) /\ SF_Vars(EnterStep)

\* Exclusive occupancy: whoever is in the hoistway is the recorded permit
\* holder and holds a permit stamped with the epoch in force -- and the
\* record names at most one car.
ShaftHeldUnderLivePermit ==
    \A c \in inShaft : holder = c /\ permit[c] = epoch

\* Progress: the express hoistway does not sit unused forever.
ShaftEventuallyUsed == <>(ran # {})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB, carC}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    NoCar = nocar

INVARIANT ShaftHeldUnderLivePermit
PROPERTY ShaftEventuallyUsed

\* Once every car has made its run and the epoch budget is spent the bank is
\* quiescent, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank has one express hoistway that bypasses the low floors. The hoistway is the critical resource: exactly one car may be inside it at a time, and a car inside it must be the car the bank currently means to be there.

Which cars are eligible for the express hoistway is set by a dispatch configuration carrying an epoch number. Republishing the configuration names a new, non-empty eligible set and advances the epoch; it is only allowed while the hoistway is empty.

The bank issues express permits one at a time. When no permit is outstanding, the bank may issue one to an eligible car that has not yet made its express run: the car is recorded as the permit holder and the permit is stamped with the epoch in force. A car may enter the hoistway if it is still the recorded permit holder and the epoch stamped on its permit is still the epoch in force. A car inside the hoistway leaves it by completing its run, which clears the outstanding permit and records the car as having made its express run.

Cars can be slow but they do not fail. A car that has been issued a permit may take a long time to get to the hoistway door, and while it dawdles the bank may withdraw the permit, and it never leaves a permit outstanding indefinitely -- the recorded holder is cleared, but nothing reaches the car, which is still moving towards the door believing its permit is good. The configuration may also be republished in the meantime, which leaves the dawdling car's permit stamped with a superseded epoch.

So a car arriving at the door may be holding a permit that is no longer recorded in its name, or one stamped with an epoch that has since been superseded, or both, and neither of those cars may be let in.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car inside the express hoistway is the car currently recorded as the permit holder and holds a permit stamped with the epoch currently in force.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The express hoistway is eventually used -- some car eventually completes an express run.

---- MODULE W4Od3m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Books, Codes, Workers, MaxSeq, NoWorker, NoAck

Accounts == Books \X Codes

BookOf(a) == a[1]

VARIABLES bookHandle, acctHandle, posting, seqOf, ack

Vars == <<bookHandle, acctHandle, posting, seqOf, ack>>

HoldsBook(w) == \E b \in Books : bookHandle[b] = w

Rooms(b) == {a \in Accounts : BookOf(a) = b}

TypeOK ==
    /\ bookHandle \in [Books -> {NoWorker} \union Workers]
    /\ acctHandle \in [Accounts -> {NoWorker} \union Workers]
    /\ posting \in [Accounts -> {NoWorker} \union Workers]
    /\ seqOf \in [Accounts -> 0..MaxSeq]
    /\ ack \in [Workers -> {NoAck} \union [acct: Accounts, sq: 0..MaxSeq]]

Init ==
    /\ bookHandle = [b \in Books |-> NoWorker]
    /\ acctHandle = [a \in Accounts |-> NoWorker]
    /\ posting = [a \in Accounts |-> NoWorker]
    /\ seqOf = [a \in Accounts |-> 0]
    /\ ack = [w \in Workers |-> NoAck]

TakeBook(w, b) ==
    /\ bookHandle[b] = NoWorker /\ ~HoldsBook(w)
    /\ bookHandle' = [bookHandle EXCEPT ![b] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acctHandle, posting, seqOf, ack>>

\* Coarse before fine: the account handle is only reachable through the book
\* handle, and the grant goes out on the wire stamped with the new sequence.
RequestAccount(w, a) ==
    /\ bookHandle[BookOf(a)] = w /\ acctHandle[a] = NoWorker
    /\ ack[w] = NoAck /\ seqOf[a] < MaxSeq
    /\ acctHandle' = [acctHandle EXCEPT ![a] = w]
    /\ seqOf' = [seqOf EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![w] = [acct |-> a, sq |-> seqOf[a] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookHandle, posting>>

\* The stamp is the whole of the test; nothing re-checks the handles here.
BeginPosting(w) ==
    /\ ack[w] # NoAck /\ ack[w].sq = seqOf[ack[w].acct]
    /\ posting' = [posting EXCEPT ![ack[w].acct] = w]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![w] = NoAck]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookHandle, acctHandle, seqOf>>

FinishPosting(a) ==
    /\ posting[a] # NoWorker /\ seqOf[a] < MaxSeq
    /\ posting' = [posting EXCEPT ![a] = NoWorker]
    /\ acctHandle' = [acctHandle EXCEPT ![a] = NoWorker]
    /\ seqOf' = [seqOf EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookHandle, ack>>

ReleaseAccount(w, a) ==
    /\ acctHandle[a] = w /\ posting[a] = NoWorker /\ seqOf[a] < MaxSeq
    /\ acctHandle' = [acctHandle EXCEPT ![a] = NoWorker]
    /\ seqOf' = [seqOf EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookHandle, posting, ack>>

\* Fine before coarse, and the release invalidates every grant in the book.
ReleaseBook(w, b) ==
    /\ bookHandle[b] = w
    /\ \A a \in Rooms(b) : acctHandle[a] = NoWorker /\ seqOf[a] < MaxSeq
    /\ bookHandle' = [bookHandle EXCEPT ![b] = NoWorker]
    /\ seqOf' = [a \in Accounts |-> IF BookOf(a) = b THEN seqOf[a] + 1
                                    ELSE seqOf[a]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acctHandle, posting, ack>>

DiscardAck(w) ==
    /\ ack[w] # NoAck /\ ack[w].sq # seqOf[ack[w].acct]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![w] = NoAck]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookHandle, acctHandle, posting, seqOf>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers, b \in Books : TakeBook(w, b) \/ ReleaseBook(w, b)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, a \in Accounts :
           RequestAccount(w, a) \/ ReleaseAccount(w, a)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : BeginPosting(w) \/ DiscardAck(w)
    \/ \E a \in Accounts : FinishPosting(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the posting engine, stated through the hierarchy: the
\* worker posting to an account holds both levels of entitlement, and each
\* level names at most one worker.
PostingHoldsBothLevels ==
    \A a \in Accounts :
        posting[a] # NoWorker =>
            /\ acctHandle[a] = posting[a]
            /\ bookHandle[BookOf(a)] = posting[a]
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Books = {bkNostro, bkVostro}
    Codes = {acMain}
    Workers = {wSettleA, wSettleB}
    MaxSeq = 3
    NoWorker = noworker
    NoAck = noack

INVARIANT PostingHoldsBothLevels

\* With every account's sequence budget spent the ledger is quiescent, which
\* is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A clearing house posts an interbank settlement batch through its ledger. The critical resource is the posting engine for a single account: exactly one settlement worker may be posting to a given account at a time, and that worker must be the one the ledger currently recognises as entitled to it.

Entitlement is held at two levels, taken coarse first then fine. Every account belongs to exactly one ledger book. A worker holding no book handle may take a free book handle. A worker holding a book handle may then request a free account handle for an account in that book; the ledger grants the account handle to that worker, advances a per-account grant sequence number, and puts a grant acknowledgement on the internal wire stamped with the new sequence number. Each worker has one acknowledgement slot, so it can have at most one grant outstanding.

The internal wire does not preserve order and the workers' acknowledgements are picked up independently, so a worker's acknowledgement can arrive long after the entitlement it refers to has been given up. A worker begins posting to an account when it picks up an acknowledgement whose stamped sequence number is still that account's current sequence number. Nothing else is checked at that point -- the sequence number is the whole of the test.

Every relinquishment advances the sequence number of the account concerned, which is what makes an old acknowledgement detectable. Finishing a posting releases the posting engine and the account handle and advances the sequence number. A worker holding an account handle it is not posting to may release just that handle, again advancing the sequence number. A worker may release a book handle only once no account handle anywhere in that book is still out -- fine before coarse. Releasing a book handle advances the sequence number of every account in that book. An acknowledgement whose stamp is not current may be discarded off the wire unread.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every account being posted to, the worker doing the posting holds both that account's handle and the handle of the book the account belongs to.

---- MODULE W4Od19m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Librarians, Requests, MaxShift, NoLib

VARIABLES duty, reading, handler, tookAt, done

Vars == <<duty, reading, handler, tookAt, done>>

Current(l) == reading[l] = duty.shift

HasWork(l) == \E q \in Requests : handler[q] = l

TypeOK ==
    /\ duty \in [shift: 0..MaxShift, roster: SUBSET Librarians]
    /\ reading \in [Librarians -> 0..MaxShift]
    /\ handler \in [Requests -> {NoLib} \union Librarians]
    /\ tookAt \in [Requests -> 0..MaxShift]
    /\ done \subseteq Requests

Init ==
    /\ duty = [shift |-> 0, roster |-> Librarians]
    /\ reading = [l \in Librarians |-> 0]
    /\ handler = [q \in Requests |-> NoLib]
    /\ tookAt = [q \in Requests |-> 0]
    /\ done = {}

\* Only a librarian on the roster in force is sent the register's contents,
\* so refreshing a reading is itself an on-duty act.
Refresh(l) ==
    /\ l \in duty.roster /\ ~Current(l)
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![l] = duty.shift]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, handler, tookAt, done>>

\* Compare-and-swap on the shift number, and nobody with work out may be
\* taken off the roster.
PublishRoster(l, rs) ==
    /\ Current(l) /\ l \in duty.roster /\ duty.shift < MaxShift
    /\ rs # {} /\ \A m \in duty.roster \ rs : ~HasWork(m)
    /\ duty' = [shift |-> duty.shift + 1, roster |-> rs]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, handler, tookAt, done>>

\* Only the reading is tested here; the roster is never consulted directly.
TakeRequest(l, q) ==
    /\ Current(l) /\ handler[q] = NoLib /\ q \notin done
    /\ handler' = [handler EXCEPT ![q] = l]
    /\ tookAt' = [tookAt EXCEPT ![q] = duty.shift]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, reading, done>>

Complete(l, q) ==
    /\ Current(l) /\ handler[q] = l
    /\ handler' = [handler EXCEPT ![q] = NoLib]
    /\ done' = done \union {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, reading, tookAt>>

\* The librarian is slow, not gone, so the desk simply takes the work back.
ReclaimRequest(q) ==
    /\ handler[q] # NoLib /\ ~Current(handler[q])
    /\ handler' = [handler EXCEPT ![q] = NoLib]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, reading, tookAt, done>>

DeskStep ==
    \/ \E l \in Librarians : Refresh(l)
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, q \in Requests : TakeRequest(l, q) \/ Complete(l, q)
    \/ \E q \in Requests : ReclaimRequest(q)

Next ==
    \/ DeskStep
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, rs \in SUBSET Librarians : PublishRoster(l, rs)

\* Roster churn is bounded by the shift budget, so weak fairness on the desk
\* work is enough once the roster settles.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(DeskStep)

\* Authorisation: no request is ever in the hands of a librarian who is not
\* on the roster now in force.
HandlersAreOnDuty ==
    \A q \in Requests : handler[q] # NoLib => handler[q] \in duty.roster

\* Progress: every request is worked off.
AllRequestsCompleted == <>(done = Requests)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Librarians = {libAsh, libBrook}
    Requests = {rqAtlas, rqQuarto}
    MaxShift = 2
    NoLib = nolib

INVARIANT HandlersAreOnDuty
PROPERTY AllRequestsCompleted

\* An empty request list with the shift budget spent is the end of the day,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A county library handles reservation requests at a desk staffed from a duty roster. The roster lives in a single shared duty register together with a shift number, and the register is only ever updated by compare-and-swap: a librarian may publish a new roster only if the shift number it last read is still the shift number in the register, and the swap advances the shift number.

Each librarian separately remembers the shift number it last read. That memory is never invalidated, so a librarian whose reading has been overtaken carries on believing the roster it read is the roster in force. Librarians are slow but they do not fail: one may sit on a request for a long time and will still eventually come back to it.

Only a librarian on the roster currently in the register is sent the register's contents, so refreshing a reading is something only an on-duty librarian can do. A librarian whose reading is current may take an unhandled request that has not already been completed, recording itself as the handler and noting the shift it took the request in. A librarian whose reading is current may complete a request it is handling, which marks the request done and leaves it unhandled again.

Publishing a new roster is subject to two conditions beyond the compare-and-swap: the new roster may not be empty, and no librarian being taken off the roster may still be handling a request. So a librarian that has work out cannot be quietly removed from under it.

Because a slow librarian's reading can be overtaken while it is still holding a request, the desk can take the request back: any request held by a librarian whose reading is no longer current is returned to unhandled.

Note that taking a request checks only that the librarian's reading is current -- it never consults the roster directly. Being on the roster is what let the librarian refresh its reading in the first place.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every request currently being handled is being handled by a librarian who is on the duty roster now in force.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every reservation request is eventually completed.

---- MODULE W4Od12m8p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Fridges, Positions, Units, Techs, NoTech, NoSlot, NoUnit

Slots == Fridges \X Positions

FridgeOf(s) == s[1]

VARIABLES storedIn, inService, fridgeHandle, slotHandle, outstanding

Vars == <<storedIn, inService, fridgeHandle, slotHandle, outstanding>>

Empty(s) == \A u \in Units : storedIn[u] # s

HoldsFridge(t) == \E f \in Fridges : fridgeHandle[f] = t

Blank == [slt |-> NoSlot, unt |-> NoUnit]

TypeOK ==
    /\ storedIn \in [Units -> {NoSlot} \union Slots]
    /\ inService \subseteq Slots
    /\ fridgeHandle \in [Fridges -> {NoTech} \union Techs]
    /\ slotHandle \in [Slots -> {NoTech} \union Techs]
    /\ outstanding \in [Techs -> [slt: {NoSlot} \union Slots,
                        unt: {NoUnit} \union Units]]

Init ==
    /\ storedIn = [u \in Units |-> NoSlot] /\ inService = Slots
    /\ fridgeHandle = [f \in Fridges |-> NoTech]
    /\ slotHandle = [s \in Slots |-> NoTech]
    /\ outstanding = [t \in Techs |-> Blank]

ClaimFridge(t, f) ==
    /\ fridgeHandle[f] = NoTech /\ ~HoldsFridge(t)
    /\ fridgeHandle' = [fridgeHandle EXCEPT ![f] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storedIn, inService, slotHandle, outstanding>>

ReleaseFridge(t, f) ==
    /\ fridgeHandle[f] = t /\ outstanding[t].slt = NoSlot
    /\ fridgeHandle' = [fridgeHandle EXCEPT ![f] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storedIn, inService, slotHandle, outstanding>>

\* Coarse before fine: a position handle is only reachable through the handle
\* of the fridge the position sits in.
ClaimSlot(t, s, u) ==
    /\ fridgeHandle[FridgeOf(s)] = t /\ slotHandle[s] = NoTech
    /\ outstanding[t].slt = NoSlot
    /\ s \in inService /\ Empty(s) /\ storedIn[u] = NoSlot
    /\ slotHandle' = [slotHandle EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![t] = [slt |-> s, unt |-> u]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storedIn, inService, fridgeHandle>>

\* Completing does not look again at whether the position is empty; the fine
\* handle held across the two steps is what keeps that true.
Complete(t) ==
    /\ outstanding[t].slt # NoSlot
    /\ slotHandle[outstanding[t].slt] = t
    /\ storedIn' = [storedIn EXCEPT ![outstanding[t].unt] = outstanding[t].slt]
    /\ slotHandle' = [slotHandle EXCEPT ![outstanding[t].slt] = NoTech]
    /\ fridgeHandle' = [fridgeHandle EXCEPT
                            ![FridgeOf(outstanding[t].slt)] = NoTech]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![t] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED inService

IssueOut(u) ==
    /\ storedIn[u] # NoSlot /\ slotHandle[storedIn[u]] = NoTech
    /\ storedIn' = [storedIn EXCEPT ![u] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, fridgeHandle, slotHandle, outstanding>>

\* An inventory-wide change, so it needs the whole coarse level quiet.
Republish(cs) ==
    /\ \A f \in Fridges : fridgeHandle[f] = NoTech
    /\ \A s \in Slots \ cs : Empty(s) /\ slotHandle[s] = NoTech
    /\ inService' = cs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storedIn, fridgeHandle, slotHandle, outstanding>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs, f \in Fridges : ClaimFridge(t, f) \/ ReleaseFridge(t, f)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, s \in Slots, u \in Units : ClaimSlot(t, s, u)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Complete(t)
    \/ \E u \in Units : IssueOut(u)
    \/ \E cs \in SUBSET Slots : Republish(cs)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No double allocation: two different units are never recorded in the same
\* storage position.
NoSharedPosition ==
    \A u1, u2 \in Units :
        (storedIn[u1] # NoSlot /\ storedIn[u1] = storedIn[u2]) => u1 = u2
====
nl:
A blood bank stores units in numbered positions inside its fridges. Every storage position takes exactly one unit, and a position must never be allocated to two units at once -- two units recorded in the same position means one of them is not really there and will be looked for in vain when it is needed.

Positions are reached through their fridge, so the technicians take the two levels in order: coarse first, then fine. A technician holding no fridge handle may claim a free fridge handle. Holding a fridge handle, and with no allocation of its own outstanding, the technician may claim the handle of a position inside that fridge, provided the position handle is free, the position is currently in service, the position is not already holding a unit, and there is a unit not yet stored anywhere; claiming records that position and that unit as the technician's outstanding allocation. A technician holding a fridge handle with no position handle out under it may simply give the fridge handle back.

To complete an allocation the technician must still hold the handle of the position it claimed. Completing records the unit as stored in that position and hands both handles back at once. Note that completing does not re-check whether the position is still empty; the position handle held across the two steps is what makes that true.

Any stored unit whose position handle is free may be issued out, which leaves the position empty again.

Capacity changes while the bank is running: the estate team republishes the set of in-service positions. Because this is an inventory-wide change it may only be done when no fridge handle anywhere is held, and no position being taken out of service may still hold a unit or still have its handle out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two different units are ever recorded as stored in the same position.

---- MODULE W4Od4m0p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Bays, Terminals, MaxVer, NoCar, NoBay

VARIABLES booked, onBay, bayVer, draft, openBays, washed

Vars == <<booked, onBay, bayVer, draft, openBays, washed>>

Blank == [car |-> NoCar, bay |-> NoBay, sawVer |-> 0]

Booked(b) == \E c \in Cars : booked[c] = b

Working(k) == draft[k].car # NoCar

TypeOK ==
    /\ booked \in [Cars -> {NoBay} \union Bays]
    /\ onBay \in [Bays -> {NoCar} \union Cars]
    /\ bayVer \in [Bays -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ draft \in [Terminals -> [car: {NoCar} \union Cars,
                  bay: {NoBay} \union Bays, sawVer: 0..MaxVer]]
    /\ openBays \subseteq Bays /\ washed \subseteq Cars

Init ==
    /\ booked = [c \in Cars |-> NoBay]
    /\ onBay = [b \in Bays |-> NoCar]
    /\ bayVer = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ draft = [k \in Terminals |-> Blank]
    /\ openBays = Bays /\ washed = {}

\* Optimistic: the terminal takes a version reading and walks away with it.
StartBooking(k, c, b) ==
    /\ ~Working(k) /\ booked[c] = NoBay /\ c \notin washed
    /\ b \in openBays /\ ~Booked(b) /\ onBay[b] = NoCar
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![k] = [car |-> c, bay |-> b,
                                      sawVer |-> bayVer[b]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, onBay, bayVer, openBays, washed>>

\* For the bay, the version comparison is the whole of the check: the commit
\* never looks again at whether the bay is still unbooked.
CommitBooking(k) ==
    /\ Working(k) /\ booked[draft[k].car] = NoBay
    /\ draft[k].sawVer = bayVer[draft[k].bay]
    /\ bayVer[draft[k].bay] < MaxVer
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![draft[k].car] = draft[k].bay]
    /\ bayVer' = [bayVer EXCEPT ![draft[k].bay] = @ + 1]
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![k] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBay, openBays, washed>>

DropStaleDraft(k) ==
    /\ Working(k) /\ draft[k].sawVer # bayVer[draft[k].bay]
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![k] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, onBay, bayVer, openBays, washed>>

RollOn(c) ==
    /\ booked[c] # NoBay /\ onBay[booked[c]] = NoCar
    /\ onBay' = [onBay EXCEPT ![booked[c]] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, bayVer, draft, openBays, washed>>

RollOff(c) ==
    /\ booked[c] # NoBay /\ onBay[booked[c]] = c
    /\ bayVer[booked[c]] < MaxVer
    /\ onBay' = [onBay EXCEPT ![booked[c]] = NoCar]
    /\ bayVer' = [bayVer EXCEPT ![booked[c]] = @ + 1]
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![c] = NoBay]
    /\ washed' = washed \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, openBays>>

\* Capacity changes under the running line, but never under a booking.
Republish(bs) ==
    /\ bs # {}
    /\ \A b \in Bays \ bs : ~Booked(b) /\ onBay[b] = NoCar
    /\ openBays' = bs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, onBay, bayVer, draft, washed>>

StartStep == \E k \in Terminals, c \in Cars, b \in Bays : StartBooking(k, c, b)

CommitStep == \E k \in Terminals : CommitBooking(k)

LineStep ==
    \/ StartStep \/ CommitStep
    \/ \E k \in Terminals : DropStaleDraft(k)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : RollOn(c) \/ RollOff(c)

Next == LineStep \/ (\E bs \in SUBSET Bays : Republish(bs))

\* The operator can keep reshuffling which bays are open, so the booking
\* steps need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(LineStep) /\ SF_Vars(StartStep) /\ SF_Vars(CommitStep)

\* No double allocation: a booked bay is either still empty or holds the very
\* car it was booked to.
BookingsMatchTheLine ==
    \A c \in Cars : booked[c] # NoBay => onBay[booked[c]] \in {NoCar, c}

\* Progress: every car gets washed.
AllCarsWashed == <>(washed = Cars)
====

\* A washed-out line with every bay's version budget spent is quiescent, not
\* deadlocked.

nl:
A car wash runs a conveyor line with a small number of wash bays. A car is first booked into a bay, then rolls onto it, then is washed and rolls off. A bay must never be allocated to two cars: if two bookings name the same bay, one of those cars will be sent onto a bay that already has a car sitting on it.

Bookings are made by a pair of booking terminals that do not coordinate. Each bay carries a version number and the terminals work optimistically. A terminal with nothing in progress starts a booking by picking a car that is not yet booked and has not yet been washed, and a bay that is open for business, not already booked to anybody and not currently occupied; it writes down that bay's version number as it stands at that moment.

To commit, the terminal requires that the car it picked is still unbooked and that the bay's version number is still the number it wrote down. If it is, the booking is recorded against the car and the bay's version advances. As far as the bay is concerned the commit does not look again at whether it is still unbooked -- the version comparison is the whole of that check. If the version has moved on, the terminal's reading is stale, and it drops the booking and starts over.

A booked car rolls onto its bay whenever that bay is empty. A car sitting on its bay is washed and rolls off: the bay goes back to empty, the booking is cleared, the car is recorded as washed, and the bay's version advances.

Capacity changes while the line is running: the operator republishes which bays are open for business. The new set may not be empty, and a bay being closed must not be booked to anybody and must not have a car on it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bay that is booked to a car is either still empty or holds that same car, so no bay is ever allocated to two cars at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car on the line is eventually washed.

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, MaxTerm, NoCtrl

VARIABLES term, lead, recalls, clearedBy, clearedAt, crashed

Vars == <<term, lead, recalls, clearedBy, clearedAt, crashed>>

Running(c) == c \notin crashed

\* `recalls[c]` is the term c remembers being elected in, and nothing ever
\* takes that memory away, so a superseded controller still believes it leads.
Believes(c) == recalls[c] = term

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm /\ lead \in {NoCtrl} \union Controllers
    /\ recalls \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ clearedBy \in [Runways -> {NoCtrl} \union Controllers]
    /\ clearedAt \in [Runways -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ term = 1 /\ lead = NoCtrl
    /\ recalls = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ clearedBy = [r \in Runways |-> NoCtrl]
    /\ clearedAt = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Sweeping the board is part of taking office: after a term change nothing
\* already on the board can be honoured.
Elect(c) ==
    /\ Running(c) /\ lead # c /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1 /\ lead' = c
    /\ recalls' = [recalls EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
    /\ clearedBy' = [r \in Runways |-> NoCtrl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clearedAt, crashed>>

\* Issuing checks the remembered term against the current one and nothing
\* else; the recognition record is never consulted here.
IssueClearance(c, r) ==
    /\ Running(c) /\ Believes(c) /\ clearedBy[r] = NoCtrl
    /\ clearedBy' = [clearedBy EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ clearedAt' = [clearedAt EXCEPT ![r] = recalls[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lead, recalls, crashed>>

ReleaseRunway(c, r) ==
    /\ Running(c) /\ Believes(c) /\ clearedBy[r] = c
    /\ clearedBy' = [clearedBy EXCEPT ![r] = NoCtrl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lead, recalls, clearedAt, crashed>>

\* Silent: no release, no hand-back of recognition, no announcement.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ Running(c) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lead, recalls, clearedBy, clearedAt>>

\* Keeps the airport moving without forcing a full election.
TowerWithdraw(r) ==
    /\ clearedBy[r] # NoCtrl /\ clearedBy[r] \in crashed
    /\ clearedAt[r] = term
    /\ clearedBy' = [clearedBy EXCEPT ![r] = NoCtrl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lead, recalls, clearedAt, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Elect(c) \/ Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways :
           IssueClearance(c, r) \/ ReleaseRunway(c, r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : TowerWithdraw(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No stale participant acts: every clearance on the board belongs to the
\* recognised lead and carries the term in force.
BoardIsCurrent ==
    \A r \in Runways :
        clearedBy[r] # NoCtrl =>
            /\ clearedBy[r] = lead
            /\ clearedAt[r] = term
====

nl:
An airport's runway allocator is run by a pool of controllers, one of whom is the recognised lead allocator at any time. Recognition is held centrally together with a term number: an election names a new lead and advances the term. Only clearances issued by the current lead under the current term may be standing on the board -- a clearance left over from a superseded lead is a runway nobody will actually release.

The board opens on term one with no lead recognised and no controller remembering any election at all. Each controller separately remembers the term in which it was last elected. That memory is never taken away from it, so a controller that has been superseded carries on believing it is the lead under the term it remembers.

An election may be called for any controller that is running and is not already the lead: the term advances, that controller becomes the recognised lead, it is told the new term, and the whole clearance board is swept clear. The sweep is part of taking office: after a term change no clearance already on the board can be honoured, including clearances belonging to a controller that is still perfectly healthy.

A running controller whose remembered term equals the current term may issue a clearance on a runway that has no clearance standing on it; the clearance is recorded against that controller and stamped with the term. Note that issuing checks only the remembered term against the current term -- it never consults the recognition record directly. A running controller whose remembered term equals the current term may also release a runway it has a clearance on, once the flight has landed.

Any controller can crash silently. A crashed controller stops doing anything at all: it does not release its runways, it does not give up recognition, and no announcement is made. To keep the airport moving without a full election, the tower may withdraw a current-term clearance that belongs to a controller which has crashed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every clearance standing on the board belongs to the controller currently recognised as lead and is stamped with the term currently in force.
